jobs.title: Regional Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
Please use Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox when accessing Candidate Home.

By joining the American Red Cross you will touch millions of lives every year and experience the greatness of the human spirit at its best. Are you ready to be part of the world's largest humanitarian network?

Join us—Where your Career is a Force for Good!

Job Description

Joining the American Red Cross is like nothing else – it’s as much something you feel as something you do. You become a vital part of the world’s largest humanitarian network. Joining a team of welcoming individuals who are exceptional yet unassuming. Diverse, yet uncompromising in unity. You grow your career within a movement that matters, where success is measured in people helped, communities made whole, and individuals equipped to never stop changing lives and situations for the better.

When you choose to be a force for good, you’ll have mentors who empower your growth along a purposeful career path. You align your life’s work with an ongoing mission that’s bigger than all of us. As you care for others, you’re cared for with competitive compensation and benefits. You join a community that respects who you are away from work as much as what you do while at work.

Where Your Career is a Force for Good!

The American Red Cross is seeking a Chief Development Officer
to support the California Gold Country Region. This region supports 31 counties in Northern California. This is a hybrid position. Incumbents will spend several days a week in the office and the remainder of their time in the field or in a home office.

What You Need To Know

In this role, you will lead a team of professional fundraisers to strengthen and grow the region’s donor base to meet its assigned financial target of more than $10M. The Chief Development Officer will provide leadership to the staff and volunteers in planning, managing, and implementing fundraising development strategies for the assigned segment(s) of giving. They will also assist in cultivating donors and sponsors to meet monthly, quarterly, and annual revenue targets while maintaining their own portfolios. The Director is responsible for managing an assigned team, including hiring, training, coaching, evaluating, and managing performance. This role is not eligible for relocation assistance.

Where Your Career Is a Force Good

Manage a portfolio of high-level donors and prospects within the assigned segment to achieve the annual revenue target, including both renewable gifts and new incremental revenue.
Develop and implement a plan for revenue growth from donors at the $5,000+ level with an emphasis on maximizing revenue for the American Red Cross. The individual segment will collaborate with the Gift Planning team to strategically grow planned giving revenue across major donor-managed accounts for individuals and families. The corporate and foundation segments’ strategic growth plan could include (but are not limited to) engagement and growth of giving societies such as the Tiffany Circle, serving as a staff liaison to the Board's Philanthropy Committee and developing and implementing strategies for board giving and influence for the region, growing cause marketing and overall corporate revenue by assisting corporations in achieving their goals to strengthen their brand, marketing, and employee engagement, leading the region's special events program, or leading a strategy to identify, cultivate, and engage foundations to grow their support for the American Red Cross.
Cultivate relationships and serve as primary staff liaison for major donors and conduct regular joint visits with relationship managers and donors when those relationships are managed by members of your team.
Collaborate with national headquarters development team members to maximize fundraising opportunities and implement policies and procedures to ensure the success of the region's fundraising efforts.
Oversee the implementation of organizational campaigns in the region.
Serve as a senior leader in the Region and proactively drive the implementation of strategic decisions for the organization. Ensure that the Region meets all reporting requirements related to fundraising, including ensuring up-to-date donor records in Salesforce.
Provide strong leadership, develop, and set individual and team performance goals and manage/drive change.
Hire, manage, train, and evaluate staff and volunteers to ensure fundraising results and that all team members meet or exceed national/regional fundraising metrics.
Lead and execute disaster relief fundraising efforts as appropriate.

What You Need To Succeed

Education:
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required.

Experience:
Minimum 7 years of sales/fundraising experience or equivalent combination of education and related experience required. Experience with increasing philanthropic revenue from diverse constituencies, developing and implementing broad-based fundraising programs, and knowledge of “best practices” in development.

Management Experience:
5 years of management experience.

Skills & Abilities:
Ability to relate well and work effectively with multiple constituencies and audiences. Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written skills. Knowledge of office systems: MS Office preferred and fundraising database systems (e.g. Raiser’s Edge, Salesforce.com). Ability to work on a team within a collaborative environment and ensure the highest customer service orientation.

Travel:
Requires frequent travel within the Region. The amount will vary depending upon size and geography of region. Occasional travel within the Division may be required.

Drive:
A current, valid driver's license and a good driving record are required.

Physical Requirements:
Physical requirements are those present in normal office environment conditions. Operational flexibility is required to meet sudden and unpredictable needs. Ability to use a personal computer, applicable software, and office equipment for sustained periods of time. May include sitting for long periods of time, driving a vehicle, and working under challenging conditions.

What Will Give You The Competitive Edge

Strong leadership/ coaching experience

Proven fundraising experience in Northern California

Effective relationship builder

Salary Information

The salary range for this position is $129,000- $142,000.

Note that the American Red Cross sets salary ranges aligned to a specific geographic location in which the work is performed. The stated salary range in this posting is an average. The specific salary information will be shared at the time of phone screening based upon your location and qualifications.

Benefits For You

As a mission-based organization, we believe our team needs great support to do great work. Our comprehensive package includes:

Medical, Dental, and Vision plans
Health Spending Accounts & Flexible Spending Accounts
PTO: Starting 15 days a year; based on type of job and tenure
Holidays: 11 paid holidays comprised of six core holidays and five floating holidays
401K with up to 6% match
Paid Family Leave Employee Assistance
Disability and Insurance: Short + Long Term
Service Awards and recognition

Apply now! Joining our team will provide you with the opportunity to

make your career a force for good!

The American Red Cross is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, San Diego Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and any other applicable state and local laws.

AmeriCorps, the federal agency that brings people together through service, and its partners — the Peace Corps, AmeriCorps Alums, National Peace Corps Association, and the Service Year Alliance — launched Employers of National Service to connect national service alumni with opportunities in the workforce. American Red Cross is proud to be an EONS partner and share our employment opportunities with the network of organizations.

Interested in Volunteering? Visit redcross.org/volunteertoday to learn more, including our most-needed volunteer positions.

jobs.description:
Details

Posted:
10-Jul-26

Location:
Diamond Bar, California

Type:
Full Time

Salary:
$275,000 - $320,000

Categories

Executive Management

Organization Overview

The Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) and Performance Racing Industry (PRI) together represent the heart of the automotive aftermarket and motorsports industries. United by a passion for cars, trucks, SUVs, and racing of every kind, these organizations support a vibrant global marketplace that spans performance parts, advanced racing technologies, restoration, restyling, and the full spectrum of specialty automotive innovation.

SEMA is a dynamic, business-minded nonprofit trade association made up of manufacturers, distributors, retailers, builders, publishers, race teams, and more—an industry ecosystem powering a nearly $53-billion-a-year retail market. Through industry-leading programs, advocacy, research, and world-class events—including the annual SEMA Show, one of the largest automotive trade shows in the world—SEMA helps its members grow, innovate, and succeed.

PRI extends this influence into the global racing marketplace. Since 1986, PRI has been the premier source of business intelligence, cutting-edge technology insights, and community connection for racing professionals. The annual PRI Trade Show in Indianapolis brings together over 1,000 exhibiting companies and thousands of racing stakeholders across every major discipline, supported by PRI’s industry-leading advocacy, media platforms, education programs, and year-round engagement.

Together, SEMA and PRI fuel the success of thousands of businesses, connect industry professionals worldwide, and preserve and grow the future of automotive performance and racing.

Purpose

Key executive leader responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the Association. This role ensures operational excellence, drives strategic initiatives, improves efficiency, and aligns operations with the Association’s long-term goals. Partners closely with the EMT to shape strategy, manage growth, and deliver exceptional organization outcomes.

Responsibilities And Authority

Provide strategic oversight of all operational functions.
Partner with respective department heads on goal development and implementation, departmental budget planning and employee development.
Establish and track key performance indicators to evaluate operational effectiveness.
Ensure teams are aligned with company values, goals, and performance expectations.
Prepare and present annual operating budget to CEO and BOD Budget Committee, in conjunction with CFO.
New Business Development – Lead the Due Diligence process for potential acquisitions. Direct and coordinate negotiations, contractual elements, financial modeling (with CFO) and implementation plan. Prepare recommendations to the CEO and BOD presentations.
Establish, monitor, evaluate and report on Annual Association Goals. Responsibilities include, preparation for CEO of periodic BOD report and Annual FY Association Goal Report for CEO and BOD leadership. (In conjunction with VP of Administration/CFO)
Develop policies, procedures, processes and programs to optimize the day-to-day operation of the Association as directed by President and CEO.
Identify potential operational risks and develop mitigation strategies, including compliance in the areas of regulation, safety, and industry-specific standards.
Participate in BOD meetings and planning sessions as a staff resource.
Lead the bi-weekly Executive Management Team meeting, including preparation and distribution of EMT report for staff distribution and drive OMP follow up actions.
Lead the operational planning and implementation of quarterly Board of Director Meetings. Determining meeting locations, hotel accommodations and agreements, F/B and ancillary activities (if applicable) with the Director of Special Events.
Perform other assignments and duties as required by CEO.

Relationships

Reports to CEO.
Interfaces with Vice Presidents/Directors/employees/Board of Directors.
Interfaces with the Association members and prospective members.

Pay Range:
$275,000 - $320,000

Skills And Knowledge Required

Excellent written and oral communication skills with proven public speaking and managerial skills.
Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks.
Bachelor’s degree in management or related discipline or an equivalent number of years of direct related experience (10-12 years).
Knowledge of the automotive aftermarket and its specialty segments is a plus.
Trade show experience (Preferred)
Proven experience with strategic planning and tracking measurable results.

This job description is not intended to be and should not be construed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities, skills, relationships or working conditions associated with the position. While it is intended to be an accurate reflection of the job requirements, management reserves the right to modify, add or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary.

Create a Job Match for Similar Jobs

About Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA)

A love for cars, trucks and SUVs is the motivating force behind the Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA). This trade association consists of a diverse group of manufacturers, distributors, retailers, publishing companies, auto restorers, street-rod builders, restylers, car clubs, race teams and more. Our organization performs many services for its members and for the hobby as a whole. Perhaps most importantly, SEMA works hard to protect consumers’ rights to drive accessorized, customized and vintage vehicles. Every year, SEMA also presents an enormous trade show in Las Vegas. This is where manufacturers unveil their latest offerings, while buyers, distributors and members of the press walk their feet off to see it all. Visit SEMAShow.com for more information.

jobs.description:
Overview

Compensation We Offer

The initial compensation for this position ranges from $117,155.00 - $144,086.00 annually, depending on experience, location and internal equity considerations.

Benefits We Offer

Benefits Eligibility starts on day ONE
We provide a robust benefits package which includes medical, dental, vision, See our Benefits Page HERE.
401K Employer Match up to 4%
Competitive Time Off Plans

Must meet eligibility requirements based on employment status

Pay Range

$117,155.00 - $144,086.00 Annually

Job Summary

Works within the vision, mission, and philosophy of the agency. Reporting to the Chief Development Officer (CDO), the Major Gifts Officer (MGO) works directly with the CDO to sustain and grow the fundraising program. The MGO will foster relationships and solicit influential/philanthropic individuals, creating enduring partnerships with Pacific Clinics (PC).PC is embarking on a comprehensive capital campaign at PC’s Hollygrove site. The MGO will play a key role in this campaign. This is a hybrid position with a flexible schedule but requiring in-person meetings with donors as well as zoom meetings, phone calls, emails, texts, etc.

Candidates with Planned Giving Experience are encouraged to apply!

Responsibilities

Develops and implements strategic plans to grow annual and major gift revenue in alignment with organizational goals.
Identifies, cultivates, solicits, and stewards a portfolio of individual donors and prospects, with a focus on major gift capacity.
Designs and manages targeted annual giving campaigns, including direct mail, digital outreach, and special appeals.
Conducts donor research and develops personalized solicitation strategies.
Partners with executive leadership and board members to support high-level donor engagement and solicitation efforts.
Oversees donor stewardship activities to ensure timely acknowledgment, recognition, and reporting.
Analyzes donor data and campaign results to inform strategy and maximize fundraising effectiveness.
Coordinates with communications and marketing teams to develop compelling donor-facing materials and messaging.
Prepares reports, dashboards, and projections to track giving trends and fundraising progress.
Maintains accurate donor records and activity tracking in donor management systems (e.g., Raiser’s Edge or RENXT).
Supports fundraising events and donor engagement initiatives as needed

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, communications, business, marketing, or related field and (8) eight or more years of relevant experience required, or equivalent combination of education and experience to include:
Minimum 7 years of experience in fundraising or development, with a strong focus on individual giving and major gifts.
CFRE Preferred.
Proven success in securing and stewarding major gifts from individuals, including face-to-face solicitation.
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute annual giving campaigns that meet or exceed revenue goals.
Strong relationship-building skills with the ability to engage, cultivate, and retain donors.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including donor-facing materials and presentations.
Proficiency in donor management and CRM systems (e.g., Raiser’s Edge, RENXT) and campaign analytics.
Strategic thinker with strong project management and organizational skills.
Ability to collaborate across departments and work closely with executive leadership.
High degree of professionalism, discretion, and commitment to donor confidentiality.
Deep understanding of philanthropic trends and best practices in donor engagement and retention.

Job Competencies

Strategic thinking and long-term planning
Relationship building and donor stewardship
Persuasive communication and solicitation skills
Data-driven decision-making and campaign analysis
Project and campaign management
Emotional intelligence and active listening
Collaboration and cross-functional coordination
Adaptability in a dynamic fundraising environment
Ethical judgment and donor confidentiality
Deep understanding of philanthropic trends and donor motivations

Physical Requirements

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand or sit. The employee is required to use their hands to produce records and/or documentation in manual or electronic formats. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 5 pounds and occasionally move or lift up to 10 pounds. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

Driving Required Will not have unsupervised contact with children. Requires full background check and TB Exam. jobs.title: Director of Advancement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha seldom find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—across a dinner table or during a conversation—told them, "This made a real difference for my child." Your responsibility is to own that word-of-mouth engine for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassador network, the relationships with civic leaders, the CEO who creates a pathway for a 14-year-old's first meaningful project.

In a typical week, you will be present in four different rooms. You will design and execute the region's event calendar, from a 150-guest open house to an intimate eight-person dinner, hosting several each month. You will identify and recruit current parents who are genuinely eager to share their experience with prospective families, and you will facilitate those one-to-one connections. You will cultivate relationships with city officials and business leaders, converting them into event venues, advocates for new campus launches, and tangible opportunities for students. And you will deliver on the Alpha Networks promise: introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internships, alumni transitions—tracked family by family.

There is no complete playbook waiting for you. You will create it as you go, and the systems you develop will be adopted by colleagues building the same infrastructure in other cities. As the region expands, the challenge intensifies rather than simplifies: the number of doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth that comes from real people advocating for Alpha, assessed over years rather than quarters.

No specific degree or credential is required. An MBA, a background in consulting or wealth management, or a self-built career in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight here. What matters is your demonstrated ability to bring people together and convert those relationships into measurable outcomes.

This role is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Evenings and weekends spent in rooms with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and entrepreneurs are standard, as is frequent local travel. You will become the most networked person in your city, and you will invest that capital in the service of students. If that exchange feels like the purpose rather than the price, you should apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and executing the region's event calendar: open gatherings, curated dinners organized by city and grade level, and family retreats, managing several per month within budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then serving as the live host for each event
Recruiting current parents to serve as ambassadors, equipping them with authentic stories, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing relationships with public officials and business executives, and converting those relationships into venues, support for campus expansion, and opportunities for students
Connecting enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and transitioning graduating families into alumni status within 30 days
Recording every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM so that "doors opened per family" reflects an accurate, trackable metric

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth through paid media, ad spend, or impression and lead-volume metrics
Controlling the brand narrative or top-level campaigns; that responsibility belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions processing, conducting tours, or managing enrollment paperwork; those are owned by Admissions and Family Success
Operating a campus on a day-to-day basis, or managing the physical facility
Treating raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the measure of success
Waiting for a completed playbook, templated materials, or support staff before beginning your work

Director Of Advancement Key Responsibilities

Drive people-first referrals as the majority source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or a comparable network business, where growth was generated through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with measurable results
Personal experience designing and executing 20+ gatherings across the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget accountability
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or business executives that resulted in concrete, identifiable value
Disciplined CRM usage; tracking relationships, attributions, and actions is an existing practice
Currently resides in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without requiring visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community building, or partnerships for a network-oriented organization: a school network, membership club, franchise, or civic or faith-based institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Rose through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were consistently chosen to host and represent the organization
Established relationships with local government or business leaders in your city
Deep understanding of how families make high-stakes educational decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $200 USD/hour, which equates to $400,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

What matters is your demonstrated ability to bring people together and convert those relationships into measurable outcomes.

This role is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Drive people-first referrals as the majority source of enrollment growth in your region.

Currently resides in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without requiring visa sponsorship

Led regional growth, community building, or partnerships for a network-oriented organization: a school network, membership club, franchise, or civic or faith-based institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Rose through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were consistently chosen to host and represent the organization
Established relationships with local government or business leaders in your city
Deep understanding of how families make high-stakes educational decisions

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

jobs.title: Managing Director & Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments
jobs.description:
Your opportunity

Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments

Overview

The Managing Director & Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments will report to the Chief Executive Officer of Schwab Asset Management and lead a team responsible for managing our expanding portfolio of non-traditional investment management offerings including the planned launch of the Schwab Private Company Fund.

Key Outcomes

This leader will be accountable for establishing the strategic direction, investment governance, operating model, and risk discipline required to scale Schwab’s private assets and alternative investments platform. The role requires sound independent judgment within approved investment guidelines, strong executive presence, and the ability to connect investment strategy, product innovation, risk management, and client outcomes across SAM/CSIM and the broader Schwab enterprise.

Set the long-term strategic agenda for Private Assets and Alternative Investments, including portfolio construction philosophy, product roadmap, governance standards, risk controls, and operating discipline across current and future offerings.
Lead the successful development, launch, and scaling of the Schwab Private Company Fund and related offerings, ensuring investment design, legal structure, compliance oversight, operations, distribution readiness, and client experience are aligned from concept through commercialization.
Make independent investment and business decisions within approved guidelines, balancing growth, liquidity, valuation, manager selection, operational complexity, fiduciary obligations, regulatory expectations, and Schwab’s reputation for client-first stewardship.
Oversee risk across the Private Assets and Alternative Investments platform, partnering closely with Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, and Technology teams to ensure strong controls, clear accountability, scalable processes, and effective issue escalation.
Serve as a senior investment and business advisor to the Chief Executive Officer of SAM/CSIM and the broader executive team, providing informed perspectives on private markets, alternative investment trends, fund performance, competitive dynamics, product opportunities, and enterprise implications.
Represent the platform with credibility before the Funds Board of Directors, SAM/CSIM committees, firm-wide risk committees, regulators, and senior enterprise stakeholders, translating complex investment, liquidity, valuation, and governance topics into clear executive-level recommendations.
Partner with leadership on the construction and oversight of SPVs serving as building blocks for the Schwab Private Company Fund, ensuring close coordination across sourcing, due diligence, structuring, valuation, operational readiness, and ongoing monitoring.
Provide leadership and expertise to third-party investment oversight and asset allocation forums involving private assets, helping shape manager due diligence, allocation recommendations, risk evaluation, and governance practices across Schwab’s expanding alternatives ecosystem.
Build, develop, and retain a high-performing team of investment professionals, portfolio managers, and research talent, strengthening bench depth, decision quality, accountability, and collaboration across an evolving and strategically important platform.
Drive medium- and long-term process improvement initiatives enhancing investment rigor, reporting transparency, regulatory readiness, operational scalability, and confidence among clients, advisors, boards, regulators, and enterprise partners.

What you have

Required Experience

15+ years of progressive senior investment leadership experience across private markets, alternative investments, asset management, portfolio construction, manager research, fund governance, or related investment disciplines.
Deep expertise investing in, allocating to, or overseeing private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, venture capital, secondaries, co-investments, hedge funds, or other alternative investment strategies, with strong judgment across multiple market cycles.
Demonstrated command of private markets portfolio construction, manager due diligence, valuation practices, liquidity management, risk oversight, investment committee governance, and ongoing monitoring of complex, less-liquid investment vehicles.
Proven knowledge of registered fund structures and regulatory requirements, including 1940 Act funds, interval funds, tender-offer funds, business development companies, registered alternatives, and other vehicles designed to broaden access to private market strategies.
Track record leading the development, approval, launch, and commercialization of new investment products, coordinating investment, legal, compliance, operations, finance, product, technology, distribution, and client-facing stakeholders through complex execution milestones.
Experience engaging with boards, regulators, senior executives, risk committees, investment committees, and external partners on investment strategy, governance, valuation, liquidity, risk controls, regulatory readiness, and client impact.
Strong understanding of the operational, legal, compliance, tax, reporting, and technology considerations required to support private assets and alternative investments at scale in a highly regulated financial services environment.
Proven people leadership capability, including the ability to recruit and develop investment talent, set clear expectations, build succession depth, strengthen team operating discipline, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, sound judgment, and continuous improvement.

Key Experiences & Ideal Profile

The ideal candidate is a seasoned private markets and alternative investments leader with the investment credibility, enterprise judgment, and executive presence to scale a strategically important platform within a complex, highly regulated financial services firm. This individual brings both strategic vision and practical execution discipline, with a demonstrated ability to set direction, lead through ambiguity, build durable governance, and translate sophisticated investment concepts into clear decisions for executives, boards, regulators, advisors, and clients.

Key leadership attributes include sound judgment, high integrity, intellectual rigor, executive presence, strong organizational discipline, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders through credibility, clarity, and trust. The leader must be comfortable operating at the intersection of investment management, product innovation, risk governance, legal and regulatory requirements, operations, distribution, and enterprise strategy while creating alignment across teams with different priorities and accountabilities.

Strategic, client-focused leader who can shape Schwab’s point of view on private assets and alternatives while maintaining disciplined stewardship, transparency, and risk management consistent with Schwab’s values.
Credible investment professional with deep private markets expertise and the ability to evaluate opportunities, risks, managers, structures, valuations, liquidity considerations, and portfolio implications with rigor and independence.
Collaborative enterprise leader who builds trusted relationships across SAM/CSIM, Schwab Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, Technology, Forge Global Advisors, SIPSS, external managers, regulators, and board-level stakeholders.
An inclusive people leader who can elevate a specialized team, develop future leaders, reinforce accountability, and create a culture that combines intellectual rigor, prudent risk-taking, operational excellence, high engagement, and continuous learning.
Decisive and balanced executive who can make sound calls amid incomplete information, competing priorities, market uncertainty, regulatory complexity, and evolving client needs while maintaining appropriate escalation, transparency, and governance discipline.
Change leader who can bring structure to ambiguity, mobilize cross-functional teams, build confidence in new investment capabilities, and guide the organization through the operational, cultural, and governance changes required to scale private assets responsibly.
Cisciplined operator who can establish scalable processes, governance routines, reporting frameworks, issue escalation protocols, and decision forums to support growth in a complex and evolving investment category.
An executive communicator who can simplify complexity, provide balanced recommendations, and represent the platform with confidence in senior leadership meetings, committee settings, board discussions, regulatory interactions, and industry forums.

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time for vacation, volunteering, and 28-day sabbatical after every 5 years of service for eligible positions
Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement
Health, dental, and vision insurance

Position Summary

Chadwick School is accepting applications for a newly created position entitled Director of Operations (DOO). The DOO is an administrative leader responsible for the strategic oversight, coordination, and continuous improvement of essential non-academic operational functions that support the mission, safety, and daily life of the school community. Serving approximately 850 students and 200 employees across a 45-acre campus, including 21 faculty/staff residential housing units, the Director helps ensure that operational services are safe, efficient, compliant, responsive, and aligned with the school's educational priorities and institutional values.

The Director of Operations reports directly to the Chief Financial Officer/Chief Operating Officer (CFO/COO) and serves as a member of the school's senior administrative leadership team. The DOO will collaborate with the Business Office, facilities department, department directors, staff, academic leaders, families, consultants, regulatory agencies, vendors, and community stakeholders to maintain a safe and thriving learning environment and to support the school's strategic priorities.

This position is designed as a strategic operational leadership role with increasing responsibility over time. Working in close partnership with the CFO/COO, the Director of Operations will assume progressively broader leadership responsibilities across the school's operational functions as part of the school's long-term leadership succession strategy.

Essential Responsibilities

Campus Safety and Security

Provide strategic leadership and oversight of all campus safety and security operations
Review, implement, and regularly evaluate comprehensive safety, emergency preparedness, and crisis response plans, and will revise as needed
Coordinate emergency drills, tabletop exercises, and incident response procedures.
Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations related to campus safety and emergency management
Serve as a member of the school's emergency response and crisis management teams.
Oversee security personnel, visitor management systems, access control systems, and campus surveillance technologies
Oversee emergency communications systems and protocols, including mass notification platforms and emergency messaging procedures
Partner with school leadership to promote a culture of safety, preparedness, and situational awareness throughout the community.

Environmental Health and Safety (EHS)

Provide support for the school's environmental health and safety programs and regulatory compliance efforts
Coordinate compliance activities related to workplace safety requirements and applicable environmental regulations
Partner with Facilities, Human Resources, Health and Academic Departments to identify, assess, and mitigate environmental and occupational risks
Support safety training initiatives and maintain appropriate documentation and reporting processes
Monitor evolving regulatory requirements and recommend operational improvements to maintain compliance and reduce risk exposure

Mail Services

Direct Liaison with representatives from USPS, FedEx, Amazon, and other services
Oversee campus mail operations, package management, and distribution systems, revising as needed in conjunction with Facilities and other departments
Ensure efficient processing and delivery of internal and external mail, parcels, and special deliveries
Develop procedures to support increasing package volumes associated with residential housing and campus operations

Food Services

Direct Liaison with onsite school dining service representatives
Partner with CFO/COO to oversee school dining services and relationships with food service providers
Monitor operational performance, food quality, customer service, and regulatory compliance in close partnership with dining service representative, facilities department and school leadership
Partner with dining provider to support student wellness initiatives, dietary accommodations, sustainability goals, and community events.
Review and manage service contracts, budgets, and operational metrics in partnership with the CFO/COO

Logistics and Campus Operations Support

Collaborate with the Facilities Director to help coordinate major operational logistics for school events, ceremonies, summer and community programs, and special initiatives
Develop systems and procedures that improve operational efficiency and service delivery
Collaborate with facilities, advancement and academic departments to support evolving campus needs

Enterprise Risk Management and Business Continuity

Partner with the CFO/COO in leading the school's enterprise risk management program
Support the identification, assessment, and monitoring of strategic, operational, financial, reputational, and compliance risks across the institution
Support the development and implementation of mitigation strategies and risk reporting processes for the senior leadership team and the Board of Trustees
Support the CFO/COO in the administration of the school's property, casualty, and commercial insurance programs, including policy renewals, broker relationships, claims management, and annual applications and regulatory filings
Completes all new and renewal applications, licensing, reports and filings to meet California and Federal guidelines
Coordinate with Human Resources to determine and manage all required employee safety and training programs
Support and coordinate the school's business continuity and disaster recovery planning program in partnership with the Head of School, CFO/COO and senior leadership
Coordinate continuity planning among operational departments and ensure preparedness for disruptions affecting campus operations or educational programs
Support resilience initiatives that strengthen the school's ability to respond to and recover from emergencies and significant operational disruptions

Conditional Use Permit (CUP)

Work closely with Head of School, CFO/COO and school leadership to support CUP efforts
Coordinate operational compliance activities associated with the school's Conditional Use Permit and related LA County and municipal agreements including car counting/reporting and resolving violations
Review and track permit requirements, operational restrictions, reporting obligations, and renewal timelines
Collaborate with school leadership, consultants, legal counsel, and local agencies regarding permit-related matters
Support documentation, community communication, and reporting requirements associated with entitlement obligations

Community and Neighborhood Relations

Serve as the school's primary operational liaison to the adjacent Homeowners Association and neighborhood stakeholders
Foster collaborative relationships with neighboring residents and community organizations
Address concerns related to traffic, parking, events, campus activities, and operational impacts
Participate in community meetings and represent the school's interests in a professional and collaborative manner
Support positive long-term relationships between the school and surrounding community

Budgeting and Vendor Management

Develop and manage departmental operating budgets
Establish key performance indicators and service standards for operational programs
Ensure fiscal responsibility while maintaining high-quality service delivery
Review service agreements and vendor contracts and inform CFO/COO of recommendations

Leadership and Collaboration

Supervise 3-4 operational staff and contracted service providers as assigned
Build strong partnerships across all academic and administrative departments
Provide regular operational reports, analysis and recommendations to the CFO/COO, HOS and other senior leaders, as needed
Participate in strategic planning, institutional initiatives, and long-range campus projects
Contribute to leadership discussions regarding operational strategy, risk management, and community engagement
Professional development: In consultation with the CFO/COO, attend seminars, conferences and workshops to remain current and share best practices
Complete other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business administration, operations management, public administration, risk management, education administration, or a related field
Minimum of seven to ten years of progressively responsible operational leadership experience
Demonstrated experience managing complex operational systems and multiple service functions simultaneously
Experience in risk management, emergency preparedness, environmental health and safety, and regulatory compliance
Strong project management, organizational, and analytical skills
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and relationship management abilities
Participation in the school's emergency response and incident management program is required
Collaborative Team Player
Sense of Humor

Preferred Qualifications

Proven leader with experience in an independent school, higher education institution, municipality, healthcare organization, or similarly complex organization
Experience with enterprise risk management and business continuity planning programs
Leadership role in campus safety and security
Familiarity with Conditional Use Permit requirements and community relations in educational settings
Professional certifications in emergency management, risk management, security management, business continuity, environmental health and safety, or operations leadership
Master's degree in a related field

Core Competencies

Strategic Thinking
Collaboration
Flexibility
Operational Excellence
Crisis and Emergency Management
Enterprise Risk Management
Relationship Building
Communication and Diplomacy
Regulatory Compliance
Project Management
Financial Stewardship
Problem Solving
Leadership and Team Development

Physical Requirements

The position requires regular movement throughout a large campus environment, attendance at evening and weekend events as necessary, and participation in emergency response activities during incidents and campus emergencies.

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENT

Required to lift and carry up to a maximum of 25 lbs., in a correct manner consistent with the appropriate training provided by the School.
Occasionally required to use hand to finger, handle or feel objects, touch and use tools, reach with hands and arms, climb stairs, bend, stoop, twist, lift, reach, push, pull, grasp, balance, kneel, crouch, crawl, grasp, talk, hear, and walk during the course of employment.
Walking and being outdoors for somewhat extended periods of time on a regular basis is part of the job as the school sits on 45 acres of land.
Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and an ability to adjust focus.
Will extensively use telephone, computer, copier, and other office equipment in the course of a day.

jobs.title: Program Director (Long Island City YMCA)
jobs.description:
Full-Time / Regular

$66,300 Salaried

The YMCA of Greater New York is here for all New Yorkers — to empower youth, improve health, and strengthen community. Founded in 1852, today the Y serves a diverse population of more than half a million New Yorkers who learn, grow, and thrive through programs and services at our 24 branches. Community is the cornerstone of the Y. Together, we connect active, engaged New Yorkers to build stronger communities.

To help fulfill our mission, we cultivate a culture of learning, leading, and collaboration to enhance community impact. Through our talented staff and “LEAP” career framework (Leadership, Empowerment, Accountability, Personal Growth), we are committed to a people-first approach that fosters trust, inclusion, growth, and development for all.

Being part of the YMCA Afterschool staff team is a deeply rewarding job where you support children’s learning, help build strong connections, and have a positive impact on so many in your community. At Y Afterschool, we will create a safe and fun space for kids to learn and grow, lead creative activities, and help them develop valuable skills. This is an opportunity to make a real difference and gain invaluable leadership and interpersonal experience.

The Long Island City YMCA is seeking a Program Director. Under the supervision of the Youth & Family Director, the Program Director serves as the strategic and operational leader for our Afterschool initiative. This multifaceted role requires a dynamic professional capable of managing all aspects of a successful, holistic youth development program.

Team Leadership: Supervising, mentoring, and leading a diverse staff team to deliver high-quality programming.
Program Excellence: Designing, creating, and implementing engaging and impactful programming that meets the developmental needs of all participants.
Inclusion and Mental Wellness: Prioritizing and integrating mental health support, case management, and social-emotional learning initiatives for both program participants and staff. Ensuring programming and day-to-day operations are welcoming to children of all abilities.
Operational Management: Meticulously managing site budgets, ensuring fiscal responsibility, and maintaining compliance with all contractual agreements and reporting requirements.

Key Responsibilities:

Direct programs serving the designated grade level band (K-5 or 6-8), ensuring all activities and services are age-appropriate and aligned with DYCD program requirements.
Ensure programs and services are deeply integrated into the specific community we serve and meet the diverse needs of all community members.
Develop and execute effective strategies for recruiting and retaining participants, aiming for consistently high attendance rates and sustained program engagement.
Develop and utilize quantitative measures, quality monitoring tools, and external evaluations to demonstrate program effectiveness.
Routinely analyze data and assessment results to identify trends, measure outcomes, and implement adjustments designed to continuously improve program quality and meet or exceed all established program goals.
Successfully establish, maintain, and leverage connections with local community partners, public/private funders, and external evaluators to enhance program services, increase resource availability, and ensure sustained program success.
Foster and lead staff in the implementation of comprehensive mental wellness support for both participants and families. Provide mental wellness resources to kids and families, and ensure staff are well-trained to create a supportive environment and identify participants who may benefit from mental wellness support/referrals.
Coordinate and implement a crisis plan to support various participant/family needs in conjunction with NYCPS school social workers, mental health staff, and external behavioral health providers.
Oversee the selection of an evidence-based SEL curriculum that is adaptable to a dynamic after-school setting (COMPASS Elementary or SONYC). Ensure all SEL programming is deliberate and clearly defines the specific social and emotional competencies that staff seek to develop in participants.
Manage the program budget, order all supplies in a timely manner, and track all expenses using the tools provided.
Recruit and retain a strong staff team with diverse abilities and backgrounds. Team skills and schedules must ensure that all aspects of the COMPASS program are delivered with an outstanding level of program quality.
Cultivate and maintain strong, collaborative working relationships with host school administration and staff.
Proactively coordinate and discuss planned activity schedules, particularly those related to STEAM and Literacy initiatives, to ensure alignment and integration with the host school's academic goals.
Maintain accurate program documentation as required by the Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS), Department of Health (DOH), Department of Youth & Community Development (DYCD), and YMCA of Greater New York.
Understand and communicate the YMCA’s core values and the goals of the Y Afterschool Program to participants and caregivers.
Develop and maintain positive relationships with parents/guardians and caregivers through regular communication regarding their child’s strengths and areas for growth. Manage communications regarding injuries or incidents, as needed.
Actively participate in training sessions, designated meetings, and special events.
Adhere to all Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS), Department of Health (DOH), YMCA of Greater New York, school partner, and funder standards, expectations, and regulations.

Desired Skills & Experience:

Must have one (1) of the following:
Associate’s Degree in Child Development, Elementary Education, Physical Education, Recreation, or a related field;
A New York State Children’s Program Administrator Credential;
A School-Age Child Care Credential or other Office-recognized credential specific to the school-age developmental period;
Two (2) years of college with 18 credits in Child Development, Elementary Education, Physical Education, Recreation, or a related field.

Minimum of two (2) years of direct experience working with children under the age of 13.
Minimum of one (1) year of experience in a supervisory capacity in a childcare program or related field of work.
Current Pediatrics CPR or First Aid certification preferred.
General knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Strong interpersonal skills, leadership qualities, and comfortable working with diverse youth and adults.

Benefits:

The YMCA of Greater New York offers a variety of benefits to its staff members, including retirement benefits , medical, paid time off, free YMCA membership, and more! Benefit eligibility is determined by an individual’s employment status (i.e., full-time or part-time), tenure, and/or the number of hours scheduled to work. Click here for more information.

How to Apply:
If you would like to be a member of our dynamic team, please complete our online application and submit your résumé and a thoughtful cover letter that explains your interest in the role and our organization.

If you are a current YMCA employee, please submit your application through the Internal Career Site in Cornerstone.

jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha seldom find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—across a dinner table or during a conversation—told them, "This made a real difference for my child." Your responsibility is to own that word-of-mouth engine for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassador network, the relationships with civic leaders, the CEO who creates a pathway for a 14-year-old's first meaningful project.

In a typical week, you will be present in four different rooms. You will design and execute the region's event calendar, from a 150-guest open house to an intimate eight-person dinner, hosting several each month. You will identify and recruit current parents who are genuinely eager to share their experience with prospective families, and you will facilitate those one-to-one connections. You will cultivate relationships with city officials and business leaders, converting them into event venues, advocates for new campus launches, and tangible opportunities for students. And you will deliver on the Alpha Networks promise: introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internships, alumni transitions—tracked family by family.

There is no complete playbook waiting for you. You will create it as you go, and the systems you develop will be adopted by colleagues building the same infrastructure in other cities. As the region expands, the challenge intensifies rather than simplifies: the number of doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth that comes from real people advocating for Alpha, assessed over years rather than quarters.

No specific degree or credential is required. An MBA, a background in consulting or wealth management, or a self-built career in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight here. What matters is your demonstrated ability to bring people together and convert those relationships into measurable outcomes.

This role is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. jobs.description:
Your opportunity

Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments

Overview

The Managing Director & Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments will report to the Chief Executive Officer of Schwab Asset Management and lead a team responsible for managing our expanding portfolio of non-traditional investment management offerings including the planned launch of the Schwab Private Company Fund.

Key Outcomes

This leader will be accountable for establishing the strategic direction, investment governance, operating model, and risk discipline required to scale Schwab’s private assets and alternative investments platform. The role requires sound independent judgment within approved investment guidelines, strong executive presence, and the ability to connect investment strategy, product innovation, risk management, and client outcomes across SAM/CSIM and the broader Schwab enterprise.

Set the long-term strategic agenda for Private Assets and Alternative Investments, including portfolio construction philosophy, product roadmap, governance standards, risk controls, and operating discipline across current and future offerings.
Lead the successful development, launch, and scaling of the Schwab Private Company Fund and related offerings, ensuring investment design, legal structure, compliance oversight, operations, distribution readiness, and client experience are aligned from concept through commercialization.
Make independent investment and business decisions within approved guidelines, balancing growth, liquidity, valuation, manager selection, operational complexity, fiduciary obligations, regulatory expectations, and Schwab’s reputation for client-first stewardship.
Oversee risk across the Private Assets and Alternative Investments platform, partnering closely with Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, and Technology teams to ensure strong controls, clear accountability, scalable processes, and effective issue escalation.
Serve as a senior investment and business advisor to the Chief Executive Officer of SAM/CSIM and the broader executive team, providing informed perspectives on private markets, alternative investment trends, fund performance, competitive dynamics, product opportunities, and enterprise implications.
Represent the platform with credibility before the Funds Board of Directors, SAM/CSIM committees, firm-wide risk committees, regulators, and senior enterprise stakeholders, translating complex investment, liquidity, valuation, and governance topics into clear executive-level recommendations.
Partner with leadership on the construction and oversight of SPVs serving as building blocks for the Schwab Private Company Fund, ensuring close coordination across sourcing, due diligence, structuring, valuation, operational readiness, and ongoing monitoring.
Provide leadership and expertise to third-party investment oversight and asset allocation forums involving private assets, helping shape manager due diligence, allocation recommendations, risk evaluation, and governance practices across Schwab’s expanding alternatives ecosystem.
Build, develop, and retain a high-performing team of investment professionals, portfolio managers, and research talent, strengthening bench depth, decision quality, accountability, and collaboration across an evolving and strategically important platform.
Drive medium- and long-term process improvement initiatives enhancing investment rigor, reporting transparency, regulatory readiness, operational scalability, and confidence among clients, advisors, boards, regulators, and enterprise partners.

What you have

Required Experience

15+ years of progressive senior investment leadership experience across private markets, alternative investments, asset management, portfolio construction, manager research, fund governance, or related investment disciplines.
Deep expertise investing in, allocating to, or overseeing private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, venture capital, secondaries, co-investments, hedge funds, or other alternative investment strategies, with strong judgment across multiple market cycles.
Demonstrated command of private markets portfolio construction, manager due diligence, valuation practices, liquidity management, risk oversight, investment committee governance, and ongoing monitoring of complex, less-liquid investment vehicles.
Proven knowledge of registered fund structures and regulatory requirements, including 1940 Act funds, interval funds, tender-offer funds, business development companies, registered alternatives, and other vehicles designed to broaden access to private market strategies.
Track record leading the development, approval, launch, and commercialization of new investment products, coordinating investment, legal, compliance, operations, finance, product, technology, distribution, and client-facing stakeholders through complex execution milestones.
Experience engaging with boards, regulators, senior executives, risk committees, investment committees, and external partners on investment strategy, governance, valuation, liquidity, risk controls, regulatory readiness, and client impact.
Strong understanding of the operational, legal, compliance, tax, reporting, and technology considerations required to support private assets and alternative investments at scale in a highly regulated financial services environment.
Proven people leadership capability, including the ability to recruit and develop investment talent, set clear expectations, build succession depth, strengthen team operating discipline, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, sound judgment, and continuous improvement.

Key Experiences & Ideal Profile

The ideal candidate is a seasoned private markets and alternative investments leader with the investment credibility, enterprise judgment, and executive presence to scale a strategically important platform within a complex, highly regulated financial services firm. This individual brings both strategic vision and practical execution discipline, with a demonstrated ability to set direction, lead through ambiguity, build durable governance, and translate sophisticated investment concepts into clear decisions for executives, boards, regulators, advisors, and clients.

Key leadership attributes include sound judgment, high integrity, intellectual rigor, executive presence, strong organizational discipline, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders through credibility, clarity, and trust. The leader must be comfortable operating at the intersection of investment management, product innovation, risk governance, legal and regulatory requirements, operations, distribution, and enterprise strategy while creating alignment across teams with different priorities and accountabilities.

Strategic, client-focused leader who can shape Schwab’s point of view on private assets and alternatives while maintaining disciplined stewardship, transparency, and risk management consistent with Schwab’s values.
Credible investment professional with deep private markets expertise and the ability to evaluate opportunities, risks, managers, structures, valuations, liquidity considerations, and portfolio implications with rigor and independence.
Collaborative enterprise leader who builds trusted relationships across SAM/CSIM, Schwab Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, Technology, Forge Global Advisors, SIPSS, external managers, regulators, and board-level stakeholders.
An inclusive people leader who can elevate a specialized team, develop future leaders, reinforce accountability, and create a culture that combines intellectual rigor, prudent risk-taking, operational excellence, high engagement, and continuous learning.
Decisive and balanced executive who can make sound calls amid incomplete information, competing priorities, market uncertainty, regulatory complexity, and evolving client needs while maintaining appropriate escalation, transparency, and governance discipline.
Change leader who can bring structure to ambiguity, mobilize cross-functional teams, build confidence in new investment capabilities, and guide the organization through the operational, cultural, and governance changes required to scale private assets responsibly.
Cisciplined operator who can establish scalable processes, governance routines, reporting frameworks, issue escalation protocols, and decision forums to support growth in a complex and evolving investment category.
An executive communicator who can simplify complexity, provide balanced recommendations, and represent the platform with confidence in senior leadership meetings, committee settings, board discussions, regulatory interactions, and industry forums.

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

Figure Skating in Harlem is a nonprofit organization entering its 30th anniversary of dedication to empowering girls and young women through education, leadership development, and access to opportunity through the sport of figure skating. As the organization enters a transformative period of growth—including a major capital initiative to build its own rink—we are seeking a strategic, highly organized, and proactive Director of Development to help lead and execute our fundraising efforts.

Position Summary

The Director of Development supports the Chief Growth Officer in executing the organization’s annual fundraising strategy across individual giving, institutional giving, corporate partnerships, donor stewardship, and special events. This role will serve as the operational lead for development activities and work closely with the Chief Growth Officer to support revenue growth, strengthen donor engagement, and build sustainable fundraising systems. The Director of Development will oversee all planning, coordination, and execution of the organization’s annual gala and other fundraising events, managing all pre-event logistics internally while partnering with external consultants and vendors for design support and day-of event execution. This position will also play a growing role in corporate sponsorship strategy and relationship management. Corporate partnerships will initially be a shared responsibility with senior leadership and transition more fully to this role over time. The Director of Development will work collaboratively with the organization’s Director of Communications & External Affairs to ensure alignment across fundraising, government relations, corporate engagement, communications, and institutional strategy. The role will also receive operational and administrative support from a shared Development & Operations Coordinator. The ideal candidate is strategic, highly organized, self-directed, and execution-oriented.

Key Responsibilities

Development Strategy & Revenue Execution

Partner with the Chief Growth Officer to execute the organization’s annual fundraising plan and revenue strategy, especially major donor cultivation, stewardship, and solicitation efforts
Manage timelines, deliverables, and execution across fundraising initiatives
In coordination with Chief Growth Officer, maintain and strengthen donor pipelines and moves management systems; prepare donor materials, briefing documents, proposals, and stewardship reports
Track fundraising performance and provide regular reporting and analysis
Proactively identify opportunities, challenges, and operational needs across the development function

Institutional Giving & Grants

Manage grant calendar, deadlines, reporting, and submissions for non-government funders
Draft and coordinate foundation and institutional grant proposals and reports
Maintain relationships and records for private and institutional funders
Ensure compliance with grant requirements and reporting timelines

Manage all pre-event planning, coordination, timelines, logistics, and internal execution
Oversee sponsorship outreach and fulfillment, invitation management, auction coordination, seating, vendor coordination, and event communications
Partner with external consultants and vendors on graphic design, production support, and day-of event execution
Manage post-event stewardship and donor follow-up plans
Collaborate with board members, host committees, and leadership to drive event fundraising success

Young Professionals Board Management

Manage board communications, meetings, engagement strategies, and event coordination
Support fundraising initiatives, membership cultivation, and volunteer leadership development

Corporate Partnerships

Support development and stewardship of corporate sponsorship relationships
Work collaboratively with senior leadership and the Director of Communications & External Affairs on sponsorship strategy and outreach
Over time, assume increasing ownership of corporate partnership management and revenue generation

Development Operations & Stewardship

Partner with the Development & Operations Coordinator to oversee donor acknowledgment and stewardship systems
Ensure database accuracy, gift processing integrity, and strong donor record management
Oversee gift reconciliation processes between development and finance
Improve systems and workflows to increase efficiency and donor experience

Qualifications

5-8 years of progressively responsible, nonprofit development experience
Proven experience independently managing fundraising events and complex projects
Strong writing and communication skills, including experience in grant writing

jobs.title: Program Director (La Central YMCA)
jobs.description:
Full-Time / Regular

$66,300 Salaried

The YMCA of Greater New York is here for all New Yorkers — to empower youth, improve health, and strengthen community. Founded in 1852, today the Y serves a diverse population of more than half a million New Yorkers who learn, grow, and thrive through programs and services at our 24 branches. Community is the cornerstone of the Y. Together, we connect active, engaged New Yorkers to build stronger communities.

To help fulfill our mission, we cultivate a culture of learning, leading, and collaboration to enhance community impact. Through our talented staff and “LEAP” career framework (Leadership, Empowerment, Accountability, Personal Growth), we are committed to a people-first approach that fosters trust, inclusion, growth, and development for all.

Being part of the YMCA Afterschool staff team is a deeply rewarding job where you support children’s learning, help build strong connections, and have a positive impact on so many in your community. At Y Afterschool, we will create a safe and fun space for kids to learn and grow, lead creative activities, and help them develop valuable skills. This is an opportunity to make a real difference and gain invaluable leadership and interpersonal experience.

The La Central YMCA is seeking a Program Director. Under the supervision of the Youth & Family Director, the Program Director serves as the strategic and operational leader for our Afterschool initiative. This multifaceted role requires a dynamic professional capable of managing all aspects of a successful, holistic youth development program.

Team Leadership: Supervising, mentoring, and leading a diverse staff team to deliver high-quality programming.
Program Excellence: Designing, creating, and implementing engaging and impactful programming that meets the developmental needs of all participants.
Inclusion and Mental Wellness: Prioritizing and integrating mental health support, case management, and social-emotional learning initiatives for both program participants and staff. Ensuring programming and day-to-day operations are welcoming to children of all abilities.
Operational Management: Meticulously managing site budgets, ensuring fiscal responsibility, and maintaining compliance with all contractual agreements and reporting requirements.

Key Responsibilities:

Direct programs serving the designated grade level band (K-5 or 6-8), ensuring all activities and services are age-appropriate and aligned with DYCD program requirements.
Ensure programs and services are deeply integrated into the specific community we serve and meet the diverse needs of all community members.
Develop and execute effective strategies for recruiting and retaining participants, aiming for consistently high attendance rates and sustained program engagement.
Develop and utilize quantitative measures, quality monitoring tools, and external evaluations to demonstrate program effectiveness.
Routinely analyze data and assessment results to identify trends, measure outcomes, and implement adjustments designed to continuously improve program quality and meet or exceed all established program goals.
Successfully establish, maintain, and leverage connections with local community partners, public/private funders, and external evaluators to enhance program services, increase resource availability, and ensure sustained program success.
Foster and lead staff in the implementation of comprehensive mental wellness support for both participants and families. Provide mental wellness resources to kids and families, and ensure staff are well-trained to create a supportive environment and identify participants who may benefit from mental wellness support/referrals.
Coordinate and implement a crisis plan to support various participant/family needs in conjunction with NYCPS school social workers, mental health staff, and external behavioral health providers.
Oversee the selection of an evidence-based SEL curriculum that is adaptable to a dynamic after-school setting (COMPASS Elementary or SONYC). Ensure all SEL programming is deliberate and clearly defines the specific social and emotional competencies that staff seek to develop in participants.
Manage the program budget, order all supplies in a timely manner, and track all expenses using the tools provided.
Recruit and retain a strong staff team with diverse abilities and backgrounds. Team skills and schedules must ensure that all aspects of the COMPASS program are delivered with an outstanding level of program quality.
Cultivate and maintain strong, collaborative working relationships with host school administration and staff.
Proactively coordinate and discuss planned activity schedules, particularly those related to STEAM and Literacy initiatives, to ensure alignment and integration with the host school's academic goals.
Maintain accurate program documentation as required by the Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS), Department of Health (DOH), Department of Youth & Community Development (DYCD), and YMCA of Greater New York.
Understand and communicate the YMCA’s core values and the goals of the Y Afterschool Program to participants and caregivers.
Develop and maintain positive relationships with parents/guardians and caregivers through regular communication regarding their child’s strengths and areas for growth. Manage communications regarding injuries or incidents, as needed.
Actively participate in training sessions, designated meetings, and special events.
Adhere to all Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS), Department of Health (DOH), YMCA of Greater New York, school partner, and funder standards, expectations, and regulations.

Desired Skills & Experience:

Must have one (1) of the following:
Associate’s Degree in Child Development, Elementary Education, Physical Education, Recreation, or a related field;
A New York State Children’s Program Administrator Credential;
A School-Age Child Care Credential or other Office-recognized credential specific to the school-age developmental period;
Two (2) years of college with 18 credits in Child Development, Elementary Education, Physical Education, Recreation, or a related field.

Minimum of two (2) years of direct experience working with children under the age of 13.
Minimum of one (1) year of experience in a supervisory capacity in a childcare program or related field of work.
Current Pediatrics CPR or First Aid certification preferred.
General knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Strong interpersonal skills, leadership qualities, and comfortable working with diverse youth and adults.

Benefits:

The YMCA of Greater New York offers a variety of benefits to its staff members, including retirement benefits , medical, paid time off, free YMCA membership, and more! Benefit eligibility is determined by an individual’s employment status (i.e., full-time or part-time), tenure, and/or the number of hours scheduled to work. Click here for more information.

How to Apply:
If you would like to be a member of our dynamic team, please complete our online application and submit your résumé and a thoughtful cover letter that explains your interest in the role and our organization.

If you are a current YMCA employee, please submit your application through the Internal Career Site in Cornerstone.
