jobs.description:
Start Your Adventure at Via Logic

Type
: Contract/1099

Rate:
$150-200/hour

Hours:
Initial engagement capped at 10 hours per month, with the possibility of additional approved hours as business needs evolve

Experience Required
: Minimum of 15+ years of executive leadership, strategic growth, mergers and acquisitions, or related advisory experience.

Location:
Remote, U.S.-based. Must be available for meetings and collaboration during Eastern Time business hours.

Your Route Into Ops

At Via Logic, we believe strong operations make meaningful work possible. As a growing small business supporting federal and commercial clients, our operating needs span people and talent, finance, contracts, compliance, security, delivery operations, partnerships, and internal systems. We’re looking for a seasoned fractional Chief Operating Officer to serve as a high-level strategic advisor to Via Logic’s principal and founders. This individual will provide executive guidance on organizational growth, mergers and acquisitions, strategic positioning, operational maturity, and long-term business planning. The role will work closely with leadership to assess opportunities, identify risks, advise on structure and sequencing, and help prepare the company for potential transactions, partnerships, expansion, or other significant growth initiatives. This is primarily an executive advisory engagement, with limited hands-on support for selected strategic and operational priorities based on agreed scope, available hours, and leadership needs.

Your Mission

In this role, you will provide executive-level guidance across several operating areas, with priorities selected and sequenced based on the company’s most significant strategic and operational needs.

Business Ops

Support the founders in organizing, prioritizing, and sequencing strategic and operational workstreams.
Advise on how open priorities should be structured, assigned, sequenced, monitored, and escalated.
Recommend operating rhythms, internal workflows, accountability structures, and cross-functional coordination practices.
Provide high-level review and recommendations related to delivery operations, timekeeping controls, approval workflows, audit readiness, and operational risk.
Advise leadership on enterprise-level risks and accountability related to facility clearance operations, security compliance, and DCSA obligations.
Provide limited hands-on support for selected operational projects when specifically agreed upon within the approved scope and available hours.

People & Talent

Advise on organizational structure, hiring strategy, recruiting operations, role definition, leadership capacity, and internal support needs.
Support planning around performance reviews, compensation cycles, benefits decisions, team lead structures, growth frameworks, succession planning, and workforce readiness.
Help clarify which responsibilities should sit with People/Talent, leadership, internal operations, outside advisors, or other functional owners.
Provide limited project-based support for selected People and Talent initiatives when agreed upon within the approved scope.

Expanse

Advise on vendor relationships, consultant support, strategic partnerships, and other external business relationships.
Help leadership evaluate partnership opportunities, operational dependencies, risks, ownership considerations, and expected business value.
Recommend processes for tracking and resolving material expense, vendor, consultant, or partnership-related matters.
Support the creation or refinement of selected trackers, workflows, and ownership paths when those items are prioritized within the engagement.

Finance

Provide executive-level guidance related to financial operations, bookkeeping cadence, reporting structure, profitability, forecasting, and cross-system coordination.
Support review of financial and accounting matters such as QuickBooks Online structure, Gusto coordination, chart-of-accounts alignment, project-level reporting, invoice tracking, expense processes, and year-end or forward-year planning.
Advise on financial and operational readiness for growth, investment, acquisition, sale, integration, or other significant business events.
Help identify gaps related to reporting maturity, internal controls, audit readiness, valuation readiness, and due diligence preparation.
Clarify which matters should sit with internal operations, bookkeeping support, accounting or tax advisors, legal counsel, or leadership.
Coordinate with internal team members and external finance, accounting, tax, or legal partners as needed and within the approved scope.

Contracts

Advise on operational tracking and strategic risk related to NDAs, subcontracts, contract actions, GSA MAS updates, SAM.gov requirements, and related compliance activities.
Help structure registers, trackers, ownership paths, and escalation processes for material contract and compliance matters.
Provide guidance on how government contracting requirements should be documented, assigned, monitored, and escalated.
Advise leadership on contractual, regulatory, security, and operational risks that may affect growth, partnerships, transactions, or long-term enterprise value.
Support transaction-readiness and due diligence planning related to contracts, compliance, security, and organizational risk.
Provide limited contract or compliance coordination for selected priorities when specifically assigned and agreed upon.

Because this is a limited-hours fractional engagement, priorities and any hands-on support will be reviewed, sequenced, and agreed upon with Via Logic’s principal and founders. Additional work beyond the approved monthly hours must be authorized in advance.

What Helps Explorers Succeed Here

Required Skills & Experience

15+ years of executive leadership, corporate strategy, mergers and acquisitions, transaction advisory, business integration, or equivalent experience.
Demonstrated experience advising founders, owners, boards, or executive teams through acquisitions, sales, integrations, due diligence, restructuring, or significant growth events.
Strong ability to translate broad strategic and operational needs into clear priorities, decision points, owners, risks, and recommended actions.
Experience evaluating and advising across multiple business functions, including People and Talent, finance, contracts, compliance, operations, delivery, internal systems, vendor relationships, and partnerships.
Strong executive communication, analytical, documentation, and decision-support skills.
Ability to operate independently in a fractional consulting capacity with limited hours.
Comfort advising in a fast-moving, founder-led environment where priorities may shift and organizational structure continues to evolve.
Ability to balance high-level strategic counsel with limited hands-on execution when specific priorities require it.

Strongly Preferred Skills & Experience

Prior fractional COO, executive advisory, corporate development, transaction advisory, operations consulting, investment banking, private equity operating, or M&A consulting experience.
Experience supporting founder-led, privately held, or small-to-mid-sized businesses.
Experience with transaction readiness, due diligence, valuation support, post-merger integration, restructuring, or exit planning.
Experience advising government contractors, technology companies, professional services firms, or other highly regulated businesses.
Familiarity with GSA MAS administration, SAM.gov, federal contract compliance, subcontract and NDA tracking, and related GovCon operations.
Experience assessing or supporting audit-ready financials, compliant timekeeping, project-level financial reporting, or GovCon finance operations.
Experience advising organizations that hold or support DCSA facility clearances is preferred.

Why Partner With Via Logic

Opportunity to advise a growing, founder-led small business during a meaningful stage of strategic development.
Direct collaboration with Via Logic’s principal and founders.
Ability to influence significant business, growth, operational, and organizational decisions.
Mission-driven work supporting federal and commercial programs with real-world impact.
Flexible, limited-hours fractional engagement with the potential to expand as business needs evolve.

How We Work

All Via Logic Explorers (both contractors and employees) are expected to actively engage through Slack, Teams, email, Monday.com, and other collaboration tools during standard business hours.

jobs.title: Director of Advancement
jobs.description:
Details

Posted:
28-Jul-26

Location:
Middlebury, Connecticut

Type:
Full Time

Categories:

Development/Fund Raising

Westover School (Westover), an independent, college-preparatory boarding and day school for girls in Middlebury, Connecticut, seeks a dynamic fundraiser and team leader with a proven track record to serve as its next Director of Advancement (DOA).

Reporting to the Head of School, the Director of Advancement will oversee all aspects of Westover’s fundraising, alumnae and parent engagement programs, and further strengthen a growing culture of philanthropy. With a deep belief in Westover’s mission and the transformative power of girls’ education, the Director of Advancement will help shape the strategic direction of the advancement office and position the School for its next phase of growth.

This work will be accomplished through the development and execution of a comprehensive, goal-driven advancement strategy, along with the cultivation and stewardship of meaningful, enduring relationships across the Westover community.

About Westover School

Westover School is a girls-centered boarding and day school for grades 9-12. At Westover, students are truly seen for who they are and who they aspire to be, and are celebrated for their intellect, curiosity, and unique passions. This is a community where innovative academics foster intellectual empowerment, collaboration thrives, and faculty inspire bold exploration. Rooted in sisterhood, friendships here are lifelong and unbreakable.

Since its founding in 1909, Westover has been committed to providing a transformational college preparatory education that celebrates and empowers every individual through small classes (the average class size is just 12 students) and rigorous academics (offering 21 AP and Honors Courses) within a small, close-knit community. Westover students are at the heart of their learning journeys. Creative problem-solving connected with deep intellectual curiosity is central to the school’s educational philosophy and academic vision. Today, 200 students enroll, hailing from 20 states and 24 countries. Approximately 67 percent of students identify as students of color, and 68 percent of students are boarding.

Middlebury, CT

Nestled in the picturesque town of Middlebury, Connecticut, Westover School’s 146-acre campus sits in an environment full of natural beauty, scenic landscapes, and a strong sense of community. The area is ideal for those seeking a connection to nature through easy access to myriad outdoor recreational activities, specifically those offered via Lake Quassapaug, paired with the attractions and charm of a small, quintessential New England Town. Concurrently, Middlebury has easy access to Connecticut’s major cities, including Waterbury, New Haven, and Hartford, given its proximity to I-84, and is just two hours from New York City.

Mission and Values

Westover School Embodies a Simple Yet Bold Vision:

Westover School empowers young women to lead lives of consequence.

This Is Achieved Through Four Core Values:

Strength of Character: Westover School fosters citizens of the world who are compassionate, brave, and resilient advocates for themselves and others
Women’s Empowerment: Westover empowers young women to take action as confident leaders by discovering their individual voices through exploration, reflection, and global awareness
Passion for Learning: the School champions enthusiasm and engagement as it cultivates innate curiosity into an enduring love of learning
Community: Westover nurtures an inclusive, diverse, and welcoming community rooted in tradition. Through shared experiences, Westover forges meaningful, supportive, and enduring relationships

Leadership

In partnership with Head of School Polly Fredlund, Westover is governed by an 18-member Board of Trustees and is supported by an 18-person Alumnae Board of Governors.

The Board of Trustees is composed of graduates, current and past parents, as well as other community members. As the governing body for the School, the Board of Trustees monitors Westover’s adherence to all laws and regulations, adopts policies and procedures to create a culture of legal and ethical standards that guide every aspect of the organization, and establishes bylaws and policies for effective governance and fiscal oversight. The Board conducts its work through a committee structure, which includes the following committees: Executive; Audit; Buildings and Grounds; Development; Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging; Finance; Governance; Investment; Risk Management; and Head Support.

The Board of Governors is currently comprised of graduates from 1947 to 2019. The Board of Governors’ mission is to serve as ambassadors to Westover by connecting alums, championing the Westover Fund, and advancing the mission of the school through engagement with its community. The Governors strengthen the bond between the school and alums, parents, and friends. Wherever Westover alums are, the spirit of Westover shines.

Westover further embraces the leadership strengths and contributions of the student body and provides myriad opportunities for students to fill and shape leadership roles. Among these opportunities, one of the most influential roles is the Student Heads of School. Each year, eight rising seniors are chosen by students, faculty, and staff to serve as the collective voice of the student body . The Heads of School run school assembly three times per week, serve on many committees within the School, and represent the entire student body by keeping a pulse on student life. There are two heads of school (a first and second), a diversity, equity, and inclusion head, two athletic association heads, an art head, a day student head, and a head proctor.

Financial Overview

Operating Budget $15.0M
Day Tuition $57,000
Boarding Tuition $78,500
International Tuition $82,000
Total Endowment $65.9M
Endowment per student $350,532
Annual Fund Gifts $2.3 M
Dollars raised in last campaign (Inspiring Women Campaign) $51.5M

Position Details

Advancement at Westover

Philanthropy is the cornerstone that sustains Westover beyond tuition, fueling the dreams and futures of generations to come. The generous support of Westover’s community empowers students and teachers to reach new heights of creativity, innovation, and excellence, having a profound impact that unlocks opportunities that inspire and transform. The Office of Advancement further supports the mission and strategic goals of the school by keeping alums, parents, the community, and friends connected to Westover. The most recent comprehensive campaign at Westover, the Inspiring Women Campaign, yielded $51.5M for the school, providing exceptional stability for operations and aid in building the endowment. Today, Westover benefits from 100 percent board participation, 100 percent faculty and staff participation, and a steady annual fund, which yields over $2.3M each year.

Director of Advancement

Reporting to and partnering closely with the Head of School, the Director of Advancement will serve as the strategic and tactical leader for all philanthropy and donor relations activities at Westover. In addition to the DOA, the Advancement Office at Westover currently includes a staff of five: Advancement Services Manager, Advancement Projects and Events Manager, Director of the Westover Fund, Assistant Director of Advancement - Constituent Relations, and Advancement Services Coordinator. The DOA will have the opportunity to hire additional staff once on board. The DOA will also serve as the staff liaison to the advancement committee and related subcommittees of the board of trustees and work closely with parent and alumni volunteers, in addition to serving as a key member of the Head of School’s Senior Team. Furthermore, the DOA will prioritize the following opportunities:

Opportunities

Maintain and enhance a philanthropic culture: Building upon a solid foundation of engagement and understanding, as well as through partnering with the school’s many active and dedicated volunteers, the DOA will deepen a philanthropic culture, both internally and externally. This investment will strengthen Westover’s fiscal health in both the short and long term, providing the DOA with a pivotal opportunity to shape the school’s trajectory for future generations.
Expand and diversify prospect and donor engagement: While maintaining the high engagement from faculty, staff, the board, and many alumni and parent families, the DOA will identify, cultivate, and invest in historically under-engaged constituencies, thus broadening and diversifying Westover’s prospect and donor pipeline. This includes advancing underutilized forms of giving, such as planned giving and international engagement.
Prepare and execute a comprehensive campaign: As Westover plans to launch its next comprehensive campaign, the DOA will drive its planning and execution, including aiding in defining a clear campaign vision and strategy, moving from reactive to proactive fundraising, and articulating a compelling case for support. Furthermore, the DOA will work hand-in-glove with the Head of School, ensuring that her time is utilized effectively and for the greatest impact.
Support, mentor, and develop a talented and committed team: Working with an energetic and dedicated team, the DOA will ensure role clarification, aligning responsibilities with areas of strength. The DOA will also ensure cohesion around clearly articulated goals, providing strong leadership while entrusting staff to execute.
Deepen cross-campus collaboration and partnership: The DOA will embody a collaborative leadership style and seek to enhance communication and alignment with colleagues across campus. Invest in and strengthen advancement infrastructure and data practices: Embracing data-informed goal setting, the DOA will ensure that systems and technology are utilized in a way that provides the most accurate data with ease and efficiency. They will ensure that the technology is paired with policies for accurate and timely data capture and recording, enabling more effective tracking, reporting, and strategic insight.

While Primarily An Externally Facing Role, The Next DOA Will Understand The Essentialness Of Having Connections With The Daily Life Of The School, And Will Seek To Embed Themselves To Both Aid In Supporting Westover’s Students And Then Share Their Stories With The Broader Community. Candidates Should Hold a Bachelor’s Degree, With a Master’s Degree Preferred. jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha rarely find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—sitting across a dinner table—told them, "This made a difference for our child." You will own that word-of-mouth system for an entire region: the gatherings, the parent champions, the relationship with the mayor's office, the CEO who provides a 14-year-old with their first meaningful project.

Your typical week involves four distinct environments. You create and execute the regional event calendar, ranging from 150-person open houses to eight-person curated dinners, running several each month. You identify and train current parents eager to share their experiences with prospective families, then broker one-to-one connections. You cultivate ties with municipal leaders and corporate executives, converting them into event venues, allies for campus expansions, and tangible pathways for students. And you fulfill the Alpha Networks promise: brokered introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internship placements, alumni integration, tracked meticulously family by family.

No complete playbook exists. You develop it in real time, and the frameworks you create become templates for colleagues building identical engines in other markets. As your region expands, the challenge intensifies: doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth attributable to personal endorsements, evaluated over years rather than quarters.

No degree is mandatory, and no specific background is preferred. An MBA, a career in consulting or wealth management, and a self-directed path in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight. What matters is a demonstrated history of convening people and converting relationships into outcomes.

This position is based on-site in one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. The role includes evening and weekend events with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and entrepreneurs, plus frequent local travel. You will become the most networked individual in your city, and you will invest that capital in students. If that exchange feels purposeful rather than burdensome, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and executing the regional event calendar: public open events, curated dinners segmented by city and grade level, and family retreats, multiple times per month within budget
Arranging venues, hosts, and vendors, then serving as live host during each event
Identifying current parents to serve as ambassadors, arming them with authentic narratives, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing connections with municipal officials and corporate leaders, and converting those relationships into event venues, campus launch support, and opportunities for students
Pairing enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, expert-led masterclasses, and professional internships, and integrating graduating families into the alumni network within 30 days
Recording every event, introduction, and referral source in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) to ensure "doors opened per family" is measurable and accurate

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth. No paid advertising, no media budget, no impression or lead-generation metrics
Managing brand narrative or centralized campaigns; that belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions logistics, conducting tours, or managing enrollment documentation; Admissions and Family Success own that
Operating a campus on a daily basis, or managing the physical facility
Presenting raw attendance figures and headcount as if a filled room were the objective
Waiting for a finalized playbook, a template, or additional staff before launching

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Drive people-driven referrals as the primary source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years creating communities or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or similar network businesses, where growth originated from people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client portfolio, with quantifiable results
Personally planned and executed 20+ events spanning the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ attendee open events, with full budget responsibility
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or corporate executives that delivered specific, identifiable value
Consistent CRM practitioner; tracking relationships, attributions, and activities is already standard practice
Currently resides in, or willing to relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Eligible to work in the US without requiring visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community, or partnership initiatives for a network-structured organization: a school network, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic body
Developed and leveraged a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Advanced through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and consistently served as the institutional representative and host
Pre-existing connections with local government or the business ecosystem in your city
Deep understanding of how families navigate high-stakes education choices

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $200 USD/hour, which equates to $400,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. Website Youth Empowerment Project

Empowering youth to improve their lives & the lives of others

Chief Development Officer

Job Posting

Priority Deadline: August 21, 2026

Who We Are:

Youth Empowerment Project engages underserved young people through community-based education, mentoring, employment readiness, and enrichment programs to help them develop skills and strengthen ties to family and community. YEP has served young people and families across the Greater New Orleans area for more than two decades. Through four integrated program areas, YEP provides comprehensive, community-based services grounded in the belief that support should be individualized and opportunities should be accessible to all. Each year, we serve more than 1,000 participants across 13 parishes through programs operating at different five locations. Our core purpose is to empower young people to improve their lives and the lives of others.

Our Culture And Values:

We are a community of professionals who believe in the power of collaboration, curiosity, and self-care. Our work is anchored in Respect, Kindness, and Integrity with Accountability and Progress shaping how we work. We learn continuously, invest in meaningful relationships, and care for ourselves so we can better serve one another and the young people who count on us.

The Opportunity:

The Youth Empowerment Project (YEP) is seeking an experienced, strategic, relationship-driven leader to serve as our next Chief Development Officer.

This is an exciting opportunity to join one of Greater New Orleans’ leading youth-serving organizations as we enter our next chapter of growth. Guided by a five-year strategic plan, a strong financial foundation, and an engaged Board of Directors, YEP is well positioned to build on its 21-year legacy and expand its impact for young people and families across the region.

Following a successful leadership transition from YEP’s longstanding CEO/Co-Founder, the organization has implemented a thoughtful co-leadership model with a CEO and President, designed to preserve the organization’s values, culture, and institutional knowledge while positioning it for the future. The Chief Development Officer will partner closely with both the CEO and President, joining a collaborative executive team that combines deep institutional knowledge with a shared commitment to innovation, organizational sustainability, and lasting impact for young people.

As a member of YEP’s Senior Leadership Team, the Chief Development Officer will lead the organization’s comprehensive fundraising, communications, and external engagement strategy while partnering closely with the CEO, President, and Board of Directors to grow philanthropic support and advance YEP’s mission.

The CDO will oversee and continue building a talented development team, lead fundraising strategies across individual, corporate, foundation, government, and special event revenue, and personally cultivate and develop key donor and stakeholder relationships. This leader will also help strengthen the systems, infrastructure, and culture of philanthropy that will support YEP’s continued growth for years to come.

YEP enters this next chapter from a position of organizational strength. The organization currently operates with an annual budget of approximately $5.25 million, maintains 100% Board giving,recently established an endowment, and has built significant operating reserves to help ensure long-term sustainability. Supported by an engaged, 23 member Board of Directors, a collaborative and seasoned leadership team, and a passionate and dedicated staff, the next Chief Development Officer has the opportunity to build upon a solid foundation while helping shape the future of one of the region’s leading youth-serving organizations.

This role is ideal for an experienced fundraiser who enjoys both strategic leadership and frontline fundraising. We recognize that exceptional candidates come from a variety of professional backgrounds, including Chief Development Officer, Development Director, Executive Director, CEO, and other senior leadership roles with fundraising responsibility. We welcome candidates with diverse professional backgrounds whose experience is aligned the required qualifications for this position.

We are seeking someone who thrives on building and maintaining strong relationships, collaborating with others, developing high-performing teams, and inspiring individuals and organizations to invest in a brighter future for young people in our community.

Qualifications

Link to the Full Chief Development Job Description

Bachelor’s degree required
Minimum of 7 years of senior-level leadership experience in fundraising, development, advancement, or nonprofit philanthropy, with demonstrated success leading comprehensive fundraising strategies, building high-performing teams, and securing significant philanthropic revenue. Executive leadership experience preferred.
Commitment and alignment with YEP’s mission and core values.
Team oriented collaborator who is accountable to both internal and external stakeholders
Demonstrated personal success securing significant five- and six-figure gifts and experience managing major donor, corporate, foundation, and other institutional relationships.
Proven experience developing and executing comprehensive, multi-year fundraising strategies across multiple revenue streams, with responsibility for generating and growing multi-million-dollar contributed revenue.
Experience leading, supervising, and developing teams.
Experience working effectively with executive leaders to develop and execute a fundraising strategy.
Experience working effectively with an engaged board of directors and development committee.
Experience leading fundraising campaigns, annual giving initiatives, donor stewardship efforts, fundraising events, etc.
Demonstrated ability to build sustainable fundraising infrastructure, strengthen organizational capacity, and improve development systems and processes.
Strong verbal and written communication and storytelling skills

Compensation

The salary range for this full-time position is $110,000–$135,000, commensurate with experience. We recognize that exceptional candidates bring a variety of professional backgrounds and are open to considering a range of experiences that align with the needs of the role.

YEP offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes 100% employer-paid employee health insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan with employer match, generous paid time off and 14 paid holidays, paid birthday leave, employer-paid life insurance, eligibility for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), and additional voluntary dental, vision, and disability insurance options.

OUR COMMITMENT TO EQUITY AND INCLUSION

The Youth Empowerment Project is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion in our work and on our teams. We know that the rich diversity of perspectives and wisdom that is imperative to our purpose can only come from a wide variety of origins and life experiences. We strongly believe that creating a workplace where all team members thrive is critical to fulfilling our mission in the communities we serve and we intentionally recruit, develop, and retain the most talented people from a diverse candidate pool.

Qualified candidates are urged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state, or local protected class.

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
The Moran Company is pleased to partner with Newhouse to recruit the organization's next Chief Development Officer (CDO).

Newhouse partners with domestic violence survivors to help them rise through the impacts of trauma. As the catalyst for systems change, Newhouse provides an ecosystem of transformative services that lead to safety, self-sufficiency, and whole-person healing. Guided by values of survivor-centered innovation, transformation, collaboration, excellence, integrity, and belonging, Newhouse has become one of the region's most innovative organizations serving survivors.

Over the past seven years, the organization has increased annual revenue from approximately $2.3 million to $8 million while expanding the number of individuals served by 165%. The organization is poised to enter its next transformational chapter: planning a $35 million Community Impact Campus that will redefine comprehensive services for survivors and families and deepen its impact for generations.

Newhouse is seeking a dynamic, strategic, and results-driven Chief Development Officer to lead the organization's fundraising and philanthropic growth during a transformational period of expansion. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the CDO will be responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive fundraising strategy to accelerate philanthropic growth and advance Newhouse's bold vision for the future. The CDO will be the organization's senior fundraising leader, primary major gifts officer, and a trusted thought partner to the CEO.

The CDO will lead a high-performing development team while providing strategic leadership and accountability for all fundraising efforts, including major gifts, corporate partnerships, annual giving, sponsorships, signature fundraising events, and donor stewardship. Working closely with the CEO, an engaged Board of Directors, Chief Marketing Officer, Chief Financial Officer, volunteers, donors, corporate partners, foundations, and community leaders, the CDO will strengthen relationships, inspire philanthropic investment, and foster a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization.

The Chief Development Officer will play a central role in advancing Newhouse’s vision for its first-of-its-kind Community Impact Campus by securing philanthropic support and leading innovative fundraising initiatives. This highly relational leader will build strong teams, cultivate transformational partnerships, and use compelling storytelling to generate the resources that help survivors and families heal, grow, and thrive.

The Chief Development Officer will design and execute a comprehensive, multi-year fundraising strategy that supports Newhouse’s growth, advances the $35 million Community Impact Campus, and expands major gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, events, sponsorships, planned giving, and donor stewardship. The CDO will serve as Newhouse’s lead fundraiser and philanthropic ambassador, building strong relationships with donors, foundations, corporate partners, community leaders, volunteers, and board members while collaborating with marketing and executive leadership to strengthen visibility and support. The position will also lead and develop the fundraising team, oversee development operations and CRM performance, and partner with the Chief Financial Officer on budgets, forecasts, reporting, and accountability.

The ideal candidate will hold a bachelor’s degree and bring at least seven years of progressive fundraising or nonprofit development experience, including demonstrated success with comprehensive fundraising strategies, major gifts, capital campaigns, events, donor stewardship, and team leadership. This strategic, collaborative, and mission-driven leader will possess strong communication and relationship-building skills, familiarity with donor CRM platforms, knowledge of the Kansas City philanthropic community, cultural sensitivity, reliable transportation, and the flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends.

The salary range is $120,000-$135,000, with eligibility for an annual performance-based bonus. This is a full-time, exempt position. The general schedule is Monday through Friday, plus occasional weeknights and weekends for events/planning. However, Newhouse does practice a flexible work environment if the work and key objectives are being accomplished. Newhouse pays 100% of employee health and dental benefits and matches 401(k) contributions 4% (following a 90-day qualifying period for enrollment). Newhouse offers an EAP (Employee Assistance Program), a generous PTO package starting at six weeks of PTO per year, and a two-week sabbatical after one year of employment for full-time employees. Newhouse also has an executive chef on staff and provides three hot meals to residents that shelter staff can also enjoy.

The search for the Newhouse Chief Development Officer is being conducted by The Moran Company. Questions about the position can be directed to Angie Heer at angie (at) morancompany.com. To apply for this position, submit a resume and cover letter to Angie Heer, The Moran Company, via the secure online portal. The resume should include all professional experience and examples of fundraising accomplishments. The cover letter should highlight your passion for Newhouse’s mission, relevant fundraising experience, and your approach to building a comprehensive fundraising strategy. Applications should be submitted by August 14.

Along with the Head of School, the Director of Advancement and External Affairs serves as the chief development officer and strategic advancement leader for Congressional, provides advice to the Head of School regarding fundraising priorities, and leads the advancement team. In addition to formal duties, the successful director of advancement and external affairs must be an integral member of the school community and take an active interest in the social and community-building activities of the school.

Designs, organizes, manages, and implements all capital and endowment campaigns

jobs.title: Salus Populi Program Director
jobs.description:
About the Center for Health Policy and Law:

The Center for Health Policy and Law (CHPL), “The Center” promotes innovative solutions to public health challenges at home and around the globe. The Center advances law and policy reforms to strengthen population health, reduce health disparities, nourish public health programs, and enhance access to affordable, high-quality healthcare. Housed in the School of Law and firmly rooted in Northeastern University’s nine academic colleges and international network of campuses, the Center brings together Northeastern faculty, students, and experts across disciplines to share knowledge; conduct and disseminate research; and influence the formulation and implementation of health policy and law.

About the Salus Populi:

Salus Populi: Educating the Judiciary about the Social Determinants of Health (SP) is a project in collaboration with the Center for Health Policy and Law (CHPL) at Northeastern University School of Law and the Institute for Health Equity and Social Justice Research (Institute) at Northeastern University that seeks to provide guidance and training to judges and lawyers on the impact of the law on the social determinants of health (SDOH). Funded by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation (RWJF) and the Kellogg Foundation (Kellogg), CHPL has received grants to train judges about the SDOH, with the goal of moving judges to render decisions that support health equity. The program also trains lawyers and other court personnels. The SP judicial education program is a tuition-free, interactive, and discussion-oriented course that provides judges with the tools they need to recognize how the SDOH impact the issues that come before courts and to read and evaluate public health research relating to the SDOH. The program is offered in Boston and virtually, and other locations with local partners, like San Francisco, Cleveland and North Dakota.
Since its start, SP has trained over 2100 attendees from all over the country. The team consists of faculty and staff from both CHPL and the Institute.

Position Summary:

CHPL is seeking a Program Director to oversee projects and deliverables within the Salus Populi (SP) portfolio. This position operates on a hybrid schedule, requiring some in-person days on the Boston campus.

The Program Director will have overall responsibility for the daily functioning of the SP program and work with other members of the SP Leadership team on all aspects of program development and implementation. The Program Director will be responsible for creating and implementing curriculum, organizing events, supervising program staff, and fostering collaboration partnerships. The Program Director will manage the budget and support the development of grant proposals, facilitate meetings, organize events, present at conferences, work with external partners, supervise staff, supervise law students and be adept at project management. The Program Director will serve the mission of SP by helping to train judges, lawyers and other court personnel on the SDOH. We are looking for an attorney who wants to be part of a team that has a passion for health equity, public health policy and law.

Continuation of the appointment beyond 11/1/27 is anticipated but remains contingent upon funding availability

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

JD or equivalent degree and at least 3 years of relevant work experience (e.g. higher education, public health, nonprofit, legal practice, government).
Extensive knowledge of public health law and health policy.
Demonstrated commitment to health equity and belonging and the ability to work with a diverse group of students, staff, and faculty.
Strong attention to detail and proven ability to successfully plan, execute, and monitor complex projects with multiple stakeholders and deliverables.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, this includes the ability to facilitate meetings, conduct presentations and draft reports and legal arguments.
Must be self-directed, able to make independent decisions.

Preferred Qualifications:

A MPH or equivalent degree
1-2 years of grant writing and administration experience.

Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities

Strategic Leadership and Supervision

Develop and implement program plan to advance the goals of current programs and initiatives
Shape and execute the strategic direction of current goals and initiatives, including fundraising efforts, with an emphasis on strategic partnerships and collaborations.
Serve as a mentor and supervisor for staff, student interns and research assistants, fostering their growth and development within the organization
Coordinate communications for the project

Organizational Management

Serve as a member of the Salus Populi leadership team
Supervise the legal research and drafting activities and deliverables for the project in collaboration with the project’s Principal Investigator
Draft and edit curricula and program materials;
Research and draft academic papers and other deliverables;
Draft other communications related to the project;
Supervise and guide legal and undergraduate research assistants;
Serve as a course instructor for most of the Salus Populi judicial and legal education program sessions.

Grant Management

Inform project development
Assist with any future grant and funding proposals
Meet with finance team at NUSL to monitor and track the budget
In collaboration with CHPL, identify and pursue opportunities for collaboration and/or funding.
Oversee grant reporting

Partnership Management

Oversee partners and collaborators, acting as the primary point of contact and liaison with SP
Strategically shape and direct content creation for the SP website and maintain a presence across social media platforms.
Oversight of relevant listservs, ensuring communications and outreach for SP

Please submit a resume, cover letter, and a list of 3 references in a single PDF file.

jobs.title: Director of Advancement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha seldom find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—across a dinner table or during a conversation—told them, "This made a real difference for my child." Your responsibility is to own that word-of-mouth engine for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassador network, the relationships with civic leaders, the CEO who creates a pathway for a 14-year-old's first meaningful project.

In a typical week, you will be present in four different rooms. You will design and execute the region's event calendar, from a 150-guest open house to an intimate eight-person dinner, hosting several each month. You will identify and recruit current parents who are genuinely eager to share their experience with prospective families, and you will facilitate those one-to-one connections. You will cultivate relationships with city officials and business leaders, converting them into event venues, advocates for new campus launches, and tangible opportunities for students. And you will deliver on the Alpha Networks promise: introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internships, alumni transitions—tracked family by family.

There is no complete playbook waiting for you. You will create it as you go, and the systems you develop will be adopted by colleagues building the same infrastructure in other cities. As the region expands, the challenge intensifies rather than simplifies: the number of doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth that comes from real people advocating for Alpha, assessed over years rather than quarters.

No specific degree or credential is required. An MBA, a background in consulting or wealth management, or a self-built career in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight here. What matters is your demonstrated ability to bring people together and convert those relationships into measurable outcomes.

This role is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Evenings and weekends spent in rooms with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and entrepreneurs are standard, as is frequent local travel. You will become the most networked person in your city, and you will invest that capital in the service of students. If that exchange feels like the purpose rather than the price, you should apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and executing the region's event calendar: open gatherings, curated dinners organized by city and grade level, and family retreats, managing several per month within budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then serving as the live host for each event
Recruiting current parents to serve as ambassadors, equipping them with authentic stories, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing relationships with public officials and business executives, and converting those relationships into venues, support for campus expansion, and opportunities for students
Connecting enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and transitioning graduating families into alumni status within 30 days
Recording every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM so that "doors opened per family" reflects an accurate, trackable metric

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth through paid media, ad spend, or impression and lead-volume metrics
Controlling the brand narrative or top-level campaigns; that responsibility belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions processing, conducting tours, or managing enrollment paperwork; those are owned by Admissions and Family Success
Operating a campus on a day-to-day basis, or managing the physical facility
Treating raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the measure of success
Waiting for a completed playbook, templated materials, or support staff before beginning your work

Director Of Advancement Key Responsibilities

Drive people-first referrals as the majority source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or a comparable network business, where growth was generated through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with measurable results
Personal experience designing and executing 20+ gatherings across the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget accountability
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or business executives that resulted in concrete, identifiable value
Disciplined CRM usage; tracking relationships, attributions, and actions is an existing practice
Currently resides in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without requiring visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community building, or partnerships for a network-oriented organization: a school network, membership club, franchise, or civic or faith-based institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Rose through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were consistently chosen to host and represent the organization
Established relationships with local government or business leaders in your city
Deep understanding of how families make high-stakes educational decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $200 USD/hour, which equates to $400,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

Job Summary

The Assistant Director of Development/Annual Fund supports all areas of the Development Office, as directed by the Director of Development & Alumni Relations, with a specific emphasis on the cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of individual donors through the Burke Annual Fund. This is a full-time, year-round position, which is annually contracted from July 1–June 30.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Responsible for meeting the Annual Fund goal set by the Board of Trustees.
Conceptualizes and executes an Annual Fund plan to maximize income and participation from a variety of constituents – parents, alumni, past parents, grandparents, faculty, staff, trustees and other friends of the school – utilizing a variety of techniques, including a major annual Day of Giving, direct mail, outreach through email, phone and texts, proposal writing, face-to-face solicitations, matching gifts, and third-party giving.
Coordinates with colleagues to thoughtfully build and steward donor relationships, and nurture a culture of giving through various communications, materials, events and gift acknowledgements.
Leads various events to include a major donor stewardship event.
Coordinates with the Assistant Director of Development, Advancement Services to segment donor lists and to ensure the data integrity of gift information, biographical and relational data in Burke’s development database, Raiser’s Edge. Executes reports and analyzes data to inform Annual Fund and major donor approaches and strategies.
Develops a robust volunteer program including parents, trustees, alums, faculty/staff and others in support of the Annual Fund, and recruits, trains and supports Annual Fund volunteers on an ongoing basis throughout the year.
Works with the Director of Development to coordinate the cultivation and stewardship of major donor prospects.
Synthesizes information from a variety of sources to develop comprehensive prospect research reports, as needed for staff and volunteers throughout the cultivation, solicitation and stewardship cycle.
Works with colleagues to support engagement with Burke alumni and is specifically responsible for executing giving programs with alumni.
Works within a small cohesive team, supporting all Development Office initiatives and events as needed, most importantly the annual auction each spring, but also including stewardship events, alumni relations activities and events, and major donor, planned giving and campaign activities.

Minimum Requirements

Education/Experience:

BA preferred
3-5 years of direct fundraising experience, preferably focused on Annual Fund efforts and in an independent school setting.
Previous experience with direct mail, email and phonathon solicitations.
Substantial experience with a development Constituent Relationship Management (CRM) database.
Experience with the Blackbaud’s Raiser’s Edge is strongly desired.
Experience with a data mining software desirable; experience with Blackbaud’s ResearchPoint preferred.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Goal-oriented, able to meet deadlines.
Possess strategic thinking and detail-oriented skills.
Ability to work well independently and as part of a collaborative team.
Excellent computer skills, with strong proficiency in Google Drive, Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel and other Office products and Google applications.
Must be able to attend weekend and evening activities, as necessary.
Possesses strong verbal and written communication skills.
Excellent interpersonal and organizational skills.

COMMITMENT TO EQUITY AND INCLUSION

At Edmund Burke School, we have a longstanding commitment to equity and inclusion. We are dedicated to hiring people of diverse backgrounds and perspectives, and we honor the dignity and worth of all people. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, physical abilities, sexual orientation, age, religion, national origin, or veteran status. We expect the values and work of prospective candidates to align with our mission on equity and inclusion. The culture of the Edmund Burke School aims to embrace differences, develop sensitivity to the perspectives of others, and prevent isolation of any one group of individuals.

Interested candidates should email a cover letter and resume to Jennifer Kozak Rawlings, Director of Development & Alumni Relations at jennifer.rawlings@burkeschool.org

About Edmund Burke School

Founded in 1968, Edmund Burke School is an independent, co-ed day school for 6th-12th grade on a city campus in Washington, DC – interweaving academic challenge, experiential learning, and civic engagement in a welcoming, inquisitive community. Long committed to progressive pedagogy, Burke centers the intellectual and creative lives of students and emphasizes active learning, responsive teaching, and engagement with the world around us. Administrators, faculty and staff bring a diversity of experiences and expertise to Burke, enjoy learning from and collaborating with one another, and commit to continual growth and professional development. Moreover, Burke adults thrive in a community where the growth and learning of young people is the collective focus and priority for all.

jobs.description:
Another Source’s client, UC Riverside
, is recruiting an Executive Director, Housing Services
to join their team in Riverside, California
. This is an onsite
leadership opportunity. Relocation assistance is available.

UC Riverside is one of the nation's leading public research universities and a federally designated Hispanic-Serving Institution known for advancing opportunity and social mobility. Serving a highly diverse student population—including a large percentage of first-generation college students—UCR is deeply committed to expanding access to higher education and creating meaningful pathways for student success.

Housing Services plays a critical role in that mission. As one of the university's largest auxiliary enterprises and a significant revenue-generating operation, the department directly impacts the student experience while supporting the university's long-term financial sustainability and strategic growth.

About this role:

This is an exceptional opportunity to lead one of UC Riverside's most visible and impactful auxiliary operations during a period of significant expansion. UCR Housing is projected to grow from approximately 10,000 to 14,000 on-campus residents by 2035
, making the Executive Director a key strategic leader in shaping the future of residential life at the university.

Reporting to the Associate Vice Chancellor for Auxiliary Services
, the Executive Director serves on the Auxiliary Services Senior Leadership Team and provides executive oversight for housing administration, occupancy management, financial planning, strategic initiatives, and daily operations. The role leads a department supporting approximately 25 career staff, 100 student employees, and four direct reports
, overseeing a housing enterprise generating approximately $93 million in annual revenue
.

Scope & Impact

Provide strategic leadership for all Housing Services administrative and operational functions.
Lead occupancy planning, contract administration, and annual rate strategy to meet enrollment demand and financial objectives.
Partner with the Associate Vice Chancellor on long-range financial modeling, reserve planning, debt management, deferred maintenance planning, and housing growth initiatives.
Guide the continued expansion of campus housing as the university adds approximately 4,000 additional beds through 2035.
Oversee a direct operational budget of approximately $5 million
while supporting the broader housing enterprise generating approximately $93 million
annually.
Direct housing assignments, billing, resident accounts, occupancy management, and contract compliance using enterprise housing systems.
Serve as the university's primary administrative lead for Public-Private Partnership (P3) housing operations and the North District-2 intersegmental housing partnership.
Ensure compliance with housing regulations, landlord-tenant requirements, state grant requirements, health and safety standards, and university policies.
Build strong partnerships with Enrollment Management, Student Affairs, Residential Education, Financial Aid, Student Business Services, UCPD, Auxiliary Facilities, and other campus stakeholders.
Lead and develop a high-performing leadership team while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and exceptional customer service.

Bachelor's degree in a related field or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Demonstrated experience managing complex budgets, financial planning, and operational performance.
Experience leading large teams through managers and developing high-performing organizations.
Strong knowledge of financial analysis, budgeting, internal controls, human resources, and risk management.
Excellent strategic planning, organizational, analytical, and project management skills.
Proven ability to collaborate across large, complex organizations while building trusted relationships.
Outstanding communication, leadership, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills.
Valid California driver's license (or ability to obtain one).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading housing operations within higher education.
Experience managing residential facilities operations and maintenance.
Experience supporting students, faculty, and staff within a university environment.
Knowledge of UC policies, systems, and administrative procedures.
Experience with emergency management or Emergency Operations Centers (EOC).
Understanding of residential housing operations, occupancy management, and landlord-tenant regulations.

$130,500 – $195,000

jobs.title: Executive Director of Paratransit Services
jobs.description:
At the MBTA, we envision a thriving region enabled by a best-in-class transit system. Our mission is to serve the public by providing safe, reliable, and accessible transportation. MBTA’s core values are built around safety, service, equity, sustainability, culture, and accessibility, and each employee that works for the MBTA performs their roles based on our vision, mission, and values. This includes attendance, participation, and contribution in local safety committee meetings as needed.

Job Summary

The Executive Director of Paratransit Services will report to the Chief Operating Officer. The incumbent will be responsible for all functions of the RIDE, the MBTA’s transportation option for individuals who are unable to use fixed-route services, including negotiating and managing service contracts, to ensure that the Authority’s paratransit services continue to meet the MBTA’s current high safety and quality standards. The ED will ensure that services are safe and reliable, that all policies and goals of the Authority are being met, and that services are offered within established budgetary guidelines. The ED will work with community groups, local and state officials, and all state and federal regulatory agencies to ensure service meets customer needs and is regulatory compliant. Additionally, the incumbent will lead the Department, focusing on improving overall productivity and efficiency and developing innovative ways to enhance the RIDE program.

Duties & Responsibilities

Responsible for the management and supervision of an operational management staff to ensure that services are delivered in a safe, efficient, and effective manner, as well as the management of private service and eligibility contractors to ensure strong performance, transparency, and adherence to contractual obligations.
Provide overall policy direction and enforcement of safety guidelines for paratransit services.
Establish KPIs, goals, and policies to improve the performance of employees and the delivery of service and reports as needed.
Review federal and state regulations regarding issues of concern to the Authority to ensure regulations are met, including all ADA-related issues.
Explore continuously new service options and services for customers to enhance services and to reduce the Authority's cost per trip.
Implement changes to service delivery and fare policies as needed
Collaborate with various Authority Departments such as Rail & Bus Operations, Service Planning, Systemwide Accessibility, and others to ensure close coordination between fixed route and paratransit services and initiatives.
Oversee all capital investment programs associated with Paratransit Services.
Expand strategic partnerships with customers, businesses, and community-based organizations.
Provide reports and presentations to MBTA Boards and senior managers on service performance, service changes, and enhancements.
Meet with public and private officials when needed to discuss Paratransit issues affecting the Authority.
Correspond and meet with members of the public regarding complaints of service and promote Paratransit Services.
Manage MBTA operation employees in the Paratransit Services group, including hiring, performance management, and development.
Remain up-to-date on and fulfill all roles and responsibilities as related to the MBTA’s Safety Plan and ensure resources are available to all staff, informing them of their roles and responsibilities in the Safety Plan.
Receive and coordinate investigation of all customer complaints, ensuring that a full investigation is conducted and appropriate follow-up is completed in a timely manner.
Inform the Chief Operating Officer and other senior leaders of any service disruptions.
Establish and maintain sound union/management relations while upholding the rights and interests of management and adhering to collective bargaining agreements.
Respond to each inquiry, whether from a customer, vendor, or co-worker, in a courteous and professional manner.
Respond, directly or through others, and/or report to work for emergencies, extreme weather conditions, or any other abnormal conditions that impair service or the safety of service, twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week.
Drive a company or personal vehicle to visit work sites and to assist at emergencies, service disruptions, and/or other events as needed.
Uphold the rights and interests of the Authority while building and maintaining an effective relationship with employees.
Assist in the management of a workforce by ensuring the fair and consistent application and strict adherence to the rules, regulations, collective bargaining agreements (if applicable), and policies of the Authority, including the EEO, Anti-Discrimination, Anti-Harassment, and Anti-Retaliation policies.
Perform all other duties and projects that may be assigned.

Additional responsibilities may include a focus on one or more departments or locations. See applicable addendum for department or location-specific functions.

Supervision

Direct supervision of a Director-level, a Deputy Director-level position, and an executive assistant who helps facilitate the day-to-day as well as long-term strategy and executes cross-functional initiatives.

Minimum Requirements & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Public Policy, Public Administration, Communications, Political Science, Engineering, Business Administration, Management, Urban Planning, or a related field.
Twelve (12) years of progressively responsible experience in implementation, management, improvement, and/or service delivery operations within the transit (or similar) industry.
Five (5) years of executive-level management experience in service delivery (director level or above).
Three (3) years of supervisory experience overseeing a major professional engineering and/or maintenance program, including responsibility for budget development, supervision of multiple bargaining units, and policy development and/or enforcement.
Demonstrated knowledge of government regulations and public administration practices related to transit and/or transportation, including DOT, FTA, etc.
High level of written and oral communication skills and experience in packaging financial analysis for board-level presentations
Demonstrated ability to effectively lead, manage, and motivate staff, particularly in a public sector environment
Knowledge of and familiarity with the Americans with Disabilities Act as it relates to transit services
Excellent communication skills and the ability to communicate with large audiences and facilitate meetings
Ability to learn quickly, take direction, and work independently, and to use creative, collaborative, and consultative approaches to resolve issues.
Strong conflict resolution, analytical, and problem-solving skills; ability to understand, interpret, and present data.
Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
Have the ability to provide internal and external customers with a courteous and professional experience
Have the ability to handle sensitive and confidential information in an appropriate manner.
Have the ability to travel to locations throughout the MBTA's service area
Demonstrated data-driven decision-making skills and a willingness to make test-and-learn hypotheses
Effective organizational, analytical, confidentiality, quantitative, writing, multi-tasking, and time management skills.
Demonstrated ability to communicate and present effectively to a diverse group of stakeholders and customers.
Experience in packaging and communicating complex projects for executive board-level presentations.
Demonstrated ability to think strategically and work in a team environment.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with a diverse workforce.
A valid driver’s license in accordance with MBTA policy.

Substitutions

A High School Diploma or GED with an additional seven (7) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
An associate degree from an accredited institution with an additional three (3) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
A master’s degree in a related subject substitutes for two (2) years of general experience.
A nationally recognized certification or statewide/professional certification in a related field substitutes for one year of experience.

Preferred Experience & Skills

Preferred Experience and Skills

Three (3) years of experience in professional contract management
Management experience with the public sector and/or the transportation industry, with a preference for prior experience in paratransit management.
Experience with process improvement and/or change management

Job Conditions

Ability to effectively read, comprehend, communicate, and respond to instructions, orders, signs, notices, inquiries, etc. in English.
Be at least eighteen (18) years of age, except if participating in an approved high school internship / co-op program.
Ability to commute to assigned work locations in the Boston, MA metro area, as required by the role.
Ability to provide internal and external customers with courteous and professional experiences.
Ability to work effectively, independently, and as part of a diverse workforce team (or supervise, if required).
Ability to uphold the rights and interests of the MBTA while building and maintaining effective relationships with employees and co-workers.
Ability to adhere to rules, regulations, collective bargaining agreements (if applicable), and policies of the MBTA, including the EEO, anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, and anti-retaliation policies.
Have a satisfactory work record for the two (2) years immediately prior to the closing date of this posting (unless if current student or recent graduate), including overall employment, job performance, discipline, and safety records (infractions and/or offenses occurring after the closing of the posting and before the filling of a vacancy may preclude a candidate from consideration for selection).
Ability to pass a Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) check, comprehensive background screening, and / or medical Clinic screening, potentially including physical examination and drug and alcohol screenings.
Ability to work all shifts and / or locations assigned, directed, or necessary for this position, including (for some transit / operations roles) up to twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week as necessary to accommodate severe weather conditions, emergencies, or any other circumstances that may potentially impact service or the safety of service.
Intern / co-op staff must be enrolled full or part-time in an accredited educational program and maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 for the entire duration of the internship / co-op. Additionally, interns / co-ops must have valid work authorization and U.S. Social Security Number prior to starting pre-employment screenings / pre-boarding, working in their positions, and throughout the duration of their program.

Summary

TITLE VI PROGRAM DIRECTOR JOB SUMMARY:

The Program Director is responsible for administering and coordinating the daily operations of the Elderly

Nutrition Center and Programs in accordance with DHHS/Administration on Aging and Title VI regulations, for

the Alabama Quassarte Tribal Town elders. This program consists primarily of a daily congregate and delivery

meal program and activities designed to improve health and social situations of the elderly. Work includes but

is not limited to; supervising program staff, including the selection, development and performance management of employees, program development and implementation of meal programs, support services, case management, transportation, and various elder activities and events.

Supervisory Responsibility

This position works under the general supervision of the Tribal Administrator. This position will oversee the

program staff and delegate responsibilities as needed.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

The following duties are typical for this classification. Incumbents may not perform all the listed duties and/or

may be required to perform additional or different duties from those set forth below to address program needs

and changing program practices.

Develop and oversee the Title VI programs and services such as the Elderly Nutrition Program

(Congregate and Home Delivered Meals), Nutrition Services Improvement Program (NSIP), Caregiver

Support, Support Services Program and Wellness Programs.

Develops, implements, and maintains program policies and procedures for the Title VI programs, as

needed.

Performs budgeting tasks, program monitoring, and evaluation.
Plans, coordinates, and oversees activities designed to improve health and social situations of senior

citizens.

Promotes cultural activities, respect and understanding of tribal elders.
Negotiates and prepares contracts or Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with vendors and service

partners.

Work together with the Tribal Administrator, Human Resources and Accounting Departments to

ensure compliance with agency policies and regulations.

Coordinate and implement plans of action to achieve program goals and objectives, i.e., conducts

needs assessment surveys to determine health and other special needs of senior citizens.

Plans and develops new programs as appropriate; develops grant proposals and responds to RFPs as appropriate.
Ensures positive customer service in all areas. Responds to complaints, taking all appropriate actions to

satisfy complaints.

Leads an effective team in the delivery of services to senior citizens.
Maintains daily, weekly, and monthly reports as required.
Establishes and maintains a professional relationship with associated programs and funding agencies

and provides outreach to the Elders.

Prepare monthly menus, which reflect the dietary requirements of elders in accordance with program

Associates Degree in Human Services or related field preferred with 3 years’ experience working with

Grant writing skills/experience preferable.
Proficient in computer skills such as MS Word, MS Excel, email, and the Internet.
Proficient in the following dimensions of center functions: food planning and preparation, purchasing,

sanitation, security, tribal policies and procedures, personnel management, recordkeeping, and

preparation of reports.

Must be able to handle the pressures of simultaneously coordinating a wide range of activities and

recommend appropriate solutions to center problems.

Must possess excellent verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills.

Conditions Of Employment

Must possess a valid Oklahoma driver’s license, good driving record, and be insurable. Must successfully pass a

pre-employment drug screening and be willing to submit to a criminal background check. Obtain and maintain

current CPR/First Aid Certification. Obtain and maintain current Food Handler’s Permit. This position may work

outside of the normal workweek.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to

Successfully Perform The Essential Functions Of This Job.

requires prolonged standing, bending, stooping, twisting, and lifting products and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds and repetitive hand and wrist motion. Work with hot, cold, and hazardous equipment as well asoperates phones, computers, fax machines, copiers, and other office equipment.
