jobs.title: Director of Advancement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha seldom find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—across a dinner table or during a conversation—told them, "This made a real difference for my child." Your responsibility is to own that word-of-mouth engine for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassador network, the relationships with civic leaders, the CEO who creates a pathway for a 14-year-old's first meaningful project.

In a typical week, you will be present in four different rooms. You will design and execute the region's event calendar, from a 150-guest open house to an intimate eight-person dinner, hosting several each month. You will identify and recruit current parents who are genuinely eager to share their experience with prospective families, and you will facilitate those one-to-one connections. You will cultivate relationships with city officials and business leaders, converting them into event venues, advocates for new campus launches, and tangible opportunities for students. And you will deliver on the Alpha Networks promise: introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internships, alumni transitions—tracked family by family.

There is no complete playbook waiting for you. You will create it as you go, and the systems you develop will be adopted by colleagues building the same infrastructure in other cities. As the region expands, the challenge intensifies rather than simplifies: the number of doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth that comes from real people advocating for Alpha, assessed over years rather than quarters.

No specific degree or credential is required. An MBA, a background in consulting or wealth management, or a self-built career in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight here. What matters is your demonstrated ability to bring people together and convert those relationships into measurable outcomes.

This role is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Evenings and weekends spent in rooms with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and entrepreneurs are standard, as is frequent local travel. You will become the most networked person in your city, and you will invest that capital in the service of students. If that exchange feels like the purpose rather than the price, you should apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and executing the region's event calendar: open gatherings, curated dinners organized by city and grade level, and family retreats, managing several per month within budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then serving as the live host for each event
Recruiting current parents to serve as ambassadors, equipping them with authentic stories, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing relationships with public officials and business executives, and converting those relationships into venues, support for campus expansion, and opportunities for students
Connecting enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and transitioning graduating families into alumni status within 30 days
Recording every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM so that "doors opened per family" reflects an accurate, trackable metric

Operating a campus on a day-to-day basis, or managing the physical facility
Treating raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the measure of success

Drive people-first referrals as the majority source of enrollment growth in your region.

5+ years building communities or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or a comparable network business, where growth was generated through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with measurable results
Personal experience designing and executing 20+ gatherings across the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget accountability
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or business executives that resulted in concrete, identifiable value
Disciplined CRM usage; tracking relationships, attributions, and actions is an existing practice
Currently resides in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without requiring visa sponsorship

Led regional growth, community building, or partnerships for a network-oriented organization: a school network, membership club, franchise, or civic or faith-based institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Rose through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were consistently chosen to host and represent the organization
Established relationships with local government or business leaders in your city
Deep understanding of how families make high-stakes educational decisions

jobs.title: Executive Director – Pennsylvania Council of Trout Unlimited
jobs.description:
Apply

Job Type

Full-time

Description

About PATU

The Pennsylvania Council of Trout Unlimited (PATU) is a 501(c)3 non-profit dedicated to conserving, protecting, and restoring Pennsylvania’s coldwater fisheries and their watersheds, especially our wild trout resources. We are a unified voice for 49 local chapters in six regions across the state and represent approximately 11,000 TU members statewide.

PATU’s two signature programs are the PA Coldwater Heritage Partnership (CHP) and Trout in the Classroom (TIC). CHP is a collaboration between PATU, PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, Foundation for Pennsylvania Watersheds, and PA Fish and Boat Commission. The CHP provides administrative support and funds mini-grants for conservation and protection of Pennsylvania’s coldwater streams. The TIC program, a partnership between PATU and the PA Fish and Boat Commission, is an interdisciplinary environmental education program in which students (grades K-12) learn about current and past impacts, management, and protection and enhancement opportunities of Pennsylvania’s watersheds and coldwater resources, while raising trout in the classroom.

Information about the PA Council of Trout Unlimited can be found at www.patrout.org. Coldwater Heritage Partnership information can be found at www.coldwaterheritage.org. Trout in the Classroom information can be found at www.patroutintheclassroom.org.

Position Summary

The Pennsylvania Council of Trout Unlimited (PATU) is seeking a full-time Executive Director to oversee the Coldwater Heritage Partnership (CHP) program. The Executive Director is responsible for providing strategic leadership, working with the PATU Executive Committee to establish long-range goals, strategies, plans and policies to support fundraising efforts, grant programs and educational activities. The next Executive Director joins at a pivotal moment, with a new 2026–2030 strategic plan under development and the opportunity to shape the Council’s next chapter.

The Executive Director leads the PATU’s involvement in the CHP, serving in the role of program director of the partnership that targets the conservation and protection of Pennsylvania’s coldwater streams that is a joint effort of PATU, the PA Fish & Boat Commission, the Foundation for Pennsylvania Watersheds, and the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.

The priorities of CHP are grant writing, mini-grant administration and reporting, coordinating the biennial Keystone Coldwater Conference and overseeing the Trout in the Classroom (TIC) program.

The Executive Director will be an energetic, self-starter with excellent writing and organizational skills, and preferably an individual who understands the DCNR grant system portal. Grant administration includes the technical skills necessary to monitor and report on grant results; the candidate will need to complete on-site assessments of the technical work completed by grantees. They will have oversight of grant qualifications, planning, and implementation.

This position offers significant independence for a candidate who brings a passion for angling, the outdoors, and coldwater conservation, supported by an engaged volunteer board and a clear performance framework. The ideal candidate has a finger on the pulse of conservation issues and can bring impactful changes within a statewide conservation organization.

The Executive Director must have a range of skills to effectively execute varied responsibilities, which include staff and program management, strategic planning, the ability to provide technical support and guidance to council, chapters, and other conservation organizations, conduct meetings and trainings, and oversee communication of the Council. PATU provides a Council-owned computer and required software for this position.

The position reports to the PATU President and the Executive Committee’s Staff Oversight Committee.

Duties And Responsibilities

Administer and manage the Coldwater Heritage Partnership (CHP) grants program.
Coordinate Keystone Coldwater Conference every other year.
Support the Coldwater Heritage Partnership Committee.
Administer and manage PATU’s support of the Trout in the Classroom (TIC) Program.
Administer PATU’s pipeline settlement grant fund in coordination with the PA Office of Attorney General, ensuring full utilization in eligible counties.
Lead and support fundraising and individual-giving development, including the annual appeal and donor cultivation, in partnership with the Development Committee.
Supervise PATU program staff and contractors, including performance management and volunteer coordination.
Provide regular written reports to the President and board; maintain timely, complete communication with funders, agency partners, chapters, and members.
Provide assistance and technical support to Trout Unlimited chapters and eligible watershed groups on the conservation and protection of Pennsylvania coldwater fisheries.
Work to educate the public and promote the conservation of PA’s coldwater streams.
Assist the Conservation Committee with administration of the Forever Wild grant program.
Serve as liaison between multiple agencies involved in PATU programs.
Administer budgets and project reports.
Additional duties as assigned by the PATU President and Executive Committee.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in biology, environmental science, nonprofit management, or related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
At least 5 years’ experience related to the duties of this position.
Nonprofit experience preferred.
Excellent people skills.
Must be self-motivated, flexible, and able to work independently, with minimal supervision.
Ability and willingness to travel statewide, including field sites not accessible by public transportation. A valid driver’s license and reliable means of transportation are required; mileage and approved travel expenses are reimbursed in accordance with PATU and grant funder policies.
Represent PATU at trade shows and other conservation and fishing related events.
Willing to work occasional nights and weekends to support directives.
Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check and required Pennsylvania child welfare clearances.
Proficient in Microsoft Office programs.
Experience with social media platforms preferred.
Basic bookkeeping knowledge or experience with QuickBooks.
Provide direct support to the PATU board of directors and committees.
Work to strengthen our relationship with the PA Fish and Boat Commission, PA Department of Conservation of Natural Resources and the Foundation for PA Watersheds.

Compensation

The salary range is $62,000–$77,000 annually; placement within the range is commensurate with the candidate’s skills and experience, current market rates and overall budget.

Priority consideration will be given to applications received by Sunday, August 9, 2026, 11:59 PM; the position will remain open until filled.

To apply, submit a resume and a cover letter describing your interest and relevant experience via the Trout Unlimited careers portal. A cover letter is required for consideration.

Salary Description

$62,000 and $77,000 + full benefit package

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
About Rise House 

Rise House provides shelter, advocacy, and supportive services for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault. With a 20-bed shelter, a strong reputation throughout Central  Arkansas, and an evolving volunteer base, the organization is entering an exciting period of renovation and expansion. Guided by an active Board of Directors with working committees, Rise House is focused on increasing its impact while ensuring every survivor has access to safety, hope, and healing. 

The Opportunity 

Rise House is seeking an experienced, relationship-driven Executive Director to lead the organization through its next phase of growth. As the chief executive officer, the Executive Director will partner closely with the Board of Directors, dedicated staff, volunteers, donors, funders, and community partners to strengthen services, ensure long-term financial stability, successfully guide the organization's upcoming renovation and expansion, and advance the organization's mission. This role requires a collaborative leader who is equally comfortable building relationships, raising funds, leading people, and managing a growing nonprofit. The Executive Director will serve as the public face of Rise House, champion its mission throughout the community, and foster a trauma-informed culture while positioning the organization for continued growth and lasting impact. 
What You’ll Do 

Leadership & Strategy 

• Provide visionary leadership that advances the mission, values, and long-term sustainability of Rise House.
• Lead the development and implementation of the Board-approved strategic plan, and work with the Board to identify priorities, evaluate progress, and position the organization for future growth.
• Guide the organization through renovation, expansion, and other strategic initiatives while maintaining uninterrupted, trauma-informed services for survivors.
• Foster a culture of compassion, accountability, transparency, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement among staff and volunteers.
• Provide executive leadership in organizational change management, ensuring staff, volunteers, and stakeholders remain informed, engaged, and aligned throughout periods of growth.

Fundraising, Grants, & Community Relations

• Lead a comprehensive fundraising program that includes grants, major gifts, corporate partnerships, sponsorships, annual giving, fundraising events, and donor stewardship.
• Provide executive leadership for the annual Masquerade Ball and other fundraising
initiatives.
• Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, foundations, businesses, civic organizations, elected officials, and community partners.
• Serve as the primary spokesperson for Rise House through public speaking, media opportunities, advocacy, and community engagement.
• Lead grant strategy and compliance, proposal development, and reporting.
• Ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local requirements, accreditation standards, confidentiality obligations, and funding requirements.
• Use organizational outcomes and data to demonstrate impact and drive continuous improvement. 

Board Partnership 

• Work in close partnership with an engaged Board of Directors and its committees to achieve strategic and organizational goals.
• Keep the Board informed through regular reports on finances, forecasts, fundraising, operations, compliance, and organizational performance.
• Support board recruitment, orientation, committee work, and long-term governance planning while maintaining appropriate governance boundaries. 

People, Operations & Finance 

• Lead, develop, and support a high-performing staff through coaching, performance management, and professional development.
• Develop and oversee the annual operating budget, ensure responsible stewardship of resources, and maintain strong internal controls and financial compliance.
• Develop succession plans and leadership development opportunities.
• Ensure effective HR practices, payroll oversight, benefits administration, and policy compliance.
• Lead long-range financial planning and revenue diversification.
• Provide executive oversight for facility renovations and capital improvement projects in partnership with the Board, architects, contractors, and project stakeholders.
• Support volunteer recruitment, engagement, and recognition. 

Community Impact 

• Strengthen partnerships with law enforcement, healthcare providers, schools, courts, social service organizations, and other agencies serving survivors.
• Increase community awareness of Rise House and advocate for policies and programs that enhance safety and support for survivors.
• Use organizational data and outcomes to evaluate effectiveness, communicate impact, and identify opportunities for continuous improvement

What We’re Looking For 

Required Qualifications 

• Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, business administration, public
administration, social work, or a related field. 
• Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible leadership experience, including
senior management responsibilities, preferably in a nonprofit, government, or human
services organization. 
• Demonstrated success in fundraising, grant management, donor cultivation, strategic
partnerships, and financial oversight. 
• Ability to work collaboratively with diverse populations and community stakeholders. 
• Experience working collaboratively with a Board of Directors and leading cross-functional teams. 
• Excellent leadership, staff oversight, communication, relationship-building, public
speaking, problem-solving, and organizational skills. 
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office, donor databases, and financial management systems. 

Preferred Qualifications 

• Experience leading or supporting capital campaigns, facility renovation or expansion projects, or other major organizational growth initiatives. 
• Knowledge of domestic violence, sexual assault, trauma-informed care, or related human services. 
• Experience administering VOCA, FVPSA, HUD, or similar grant funding. 

Compensation & Benefits 

Rise House offers a competitive compensation package based on experience and qualifications. Benefits include paid time off, retirement benefits match, health insurance reimbursement, professional development opportunities, mileage reimbursement, and other benefits available to employees. 
Why Join Rise House? 

This is a unique opportunity to lead a respected organization at a pivotal moment in its history. The next Executive Director will help shape the future of Rise House through facility expansion, stronger community partnerships, sustainable fundraising, and innovative services that will positively impact survivors and families throughout Central Arkansas for years to come. 
How to Apply 

Submit your resume and cover letter to careers@risehousearkansas.org 
Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a criminal background check

jobs.title: Fractional Chief Operating Officer/Operations Advisor
jobs.description:
Start Your Adventure at Via Logic

Type
: Contract/1099

Rate:
$150-200/hour

Hours:
Initial engagement capped at 10 hours per month, with the possibility of additional approved hours as business needs evolve

Experience Required
: Minimum of 15+ years of executive leadership, strategic growth, mergers and acquisitions, or related advisory experience.

Location:
Remote, U.S.-based. Must be available for meetings and collaboration during Eastern Time business hours.

Your Route Into Ops

At Via Logic, we believe strong operations make meaningful work possible. As a growing small business supporting federal and commercial clients, our operating needs span people and talent, finance, contracts, compliance, security, delivery operations, partnerships, and internal systems. We’re looking for a seasoned fractional Chief Operating Officer to serve as a high-level strategic advisor to Via Logic’s principal and founders. This individual will provide executive guidance on organizational growth, mergers and acquisitions, strategic positioning, operational maturity, and long-term business planning. The role will work closely with leadership to assess opportunities, identify risks, advise on structure and sequencing, and help prepare the company for potential transactions, partnerships, expansion, or other significant growth initiatives. This is primarily an executive advisory engagement, with limited hands-on support for selected strategic and operational priorities based on agreed scope, available hours, and leadership needs.

Your Mission

In this role, you will provide executive-level guidance across several operating areas, with priorities selected and sequenced based on the company’s most significant strategic and operational needs.

Business Ops

Support the founders in organizing, prioritizing, and sequencing strategic and operational workstreams.
Advise on how open priorities should be structured, assigned, sequenced, monitored, and escalated.
Recommend operating rhythms, internal workflows, accountability structures, and cross-functional coordination practices.
Provide high-level review and recommendations related to delivery operations, timekeeping controls, approval workflows, audit readiness, and operational risk.
Advise leadership on enterprise-level risks and accountability related to facility clearance operations, security compliance, and DCSA obligations.
Provide limited hands-on support for selected operational projects when specifically agreed upon within the approved scope and available hours.

People & Talent

Advise on organizational structure, hiring strategy, recruiting operations, role definition, leadership capacity, and internal support needs.
Support planning around performance reviews, compensation cycles, benefits decisions, team lead structures, growth frameworks, succession planning, and workforce readiness.
Help clarify which responsibilities should sit with People/Talent, leadership, internal operations, outside advisors, or other functional owners.
Provide limited project-based support for selected People and Talent initiatives when agreed upon within the approved scope.

Expanse

Advise on vendor relationships, consultant support, strategic partnerships, and other external business relationships.
Help leadership evaluate partnership opportunities, operational dependencies, risks, ownership considerations, and expected business value.
Recommend processes for tracking and resolving material expense, vendor, consultant, or partnership-related matters.
Support the creation or refinement of selected trackers, workflows, and ownership paths when those items are prioritized within the engagement.

Finance

Provide executive-level guidance related to financial operations, bookkeeping cadence, reporting structure, profitability, forecasting, and cross-system coordination.
Support review of financial and accounting matters such as QuickBooks Online structure, Gusto coordination, chart-of-accounts alignment, project-level reporting, invoice tracking, expense processes, and year-end or forward-year planning.
Advise on financial and operational readiness for growth, investment, acquisition, sale, integration, or other significant business events.
Help identify gaps related to reporting maturity, internal controls, audit readiness, valuation readiness, and due diligence preparation.
Clarify which matters should sit with internal operations, bookkeeping support, accounting or tax advisors, legal counsel, or leadership.
Coordinate with internal team members and external finance, accounting, tax, or legal partners as needed and within the approved scope.

Contracts

Advise on operational tracking and strategic risk related to NDAs, subcontracts, contract actions, GSA MAS updates, SAM.gov requirements, and related compliance activities.
Help structure registers, trackers, ownership paths, and escalation processes for material contract and compliance matters.
Provide guidance on how government contracting requirements should be documented, assigned, monitored, and escalated.
Advise leadership on contractual, regulatory, security, and operational risks that may affect growth, partnerships, transactions, or long-term enterprise value.
Support transaction-readiness and due diligence planning related to contracts, compliance, security, and organizational risk.
Provide limited contract or compliance coordination for selected priorities when specifically assigned and agreed upon.

Because this is a limited-hours fractional engagement, priorities and any hands-on support will be reviewed, sequenced, and agreed upon with Via Logic’s principal and founders. Additional work beyond the approved monthly hours must be authorized in advance.

What Helps Explorers Succeed Here

Required Skills & Experience

15+ years of executive leadership, corporate strategy, mergers and acquisitions, transaction advisory, business integration, or equivalent experience.
Demonstrated experience advising founders, owners, boards, or executive teams through acquisitions, sales, integrations, due diligence, restructuring, or significant growth events.
Strong ability to translate broad strategic and operational needs into clear priorities, decision points, owners, risks, and recommended actions.
Experience evaluating and advising across multiple business functions, including People and Talent, finance, contracts, compliance, operations, delivery, internal systems, vendor relationships, and partnerships.
Strong executive communication, analytical, documentation, and decision-support skills.
Ability to operate independently in a fractional consulting capacity with limited hours.
Comfort advising in a fast-moving, founder-led environment where priorities may shift and organizational structure continues to evolve.
Ability to balance high-level strategic counsel with limited hands-on execution when specific priorities require it.

Strongly Preferred Skills & Experience

Prior fractional COO, executive advisory, corporate development, transaction advisory, operations consulting, investment banking, private equity operating, or M&A consulting experience.
Experience supporting founder-led, privately held, or small-to-mid-sized businesses.
Experience with transaction readiness, due diligence, valuation support, post-merger integration, restructuring, or exit planning.
Experience advising government contractors, technology companies, professional services firms, or other highly regulated businesses.
Familiarity with GSA MAS administration, SAM.gov, federal contract compliance, subcontract and NDA tracking, and related GovCon operations.
Experience assessing or supporting audit-ready financials, compliant timekeeping, project-level financial reporting, or GovCon finance operations.
Experience advising organizations that hold or support DCSA facility clearances is preferred.

Why Partner With Via Logic

Opportunity to advise a growing, founder-led small business during a meaningful stage of strategic development.
Direct collaboration with Via Logic’s principal and founders.
Ability to influence significant business, growth, operational, and organizational decisions.
Mission-driven work supporting federal and commercial programs with real-world impact.
Flexible, limited-hours fractional engagement with the potential to expand as business needs evolve.

How We Work

All Via Logic Explorers (both contractors and employees) are expected to actively engage through Slack, Teams, email, Monday.com, and other collaboration tools during standard business hours.
Availability for meetings and collaboration between 9AM–5PM EST is expected.

About Via Logic

Via Logic LLC is an information technology partner supporting mission-driven work across DevSecOps, cloud engineering, cybersecurity, data science, and national security analytics for federal and commercial clients. Our teams help modernize complex systems through automation, secure engineering practices, cloud-native technologies, and scalable infrastructure solutions that support real-world impact. But beyond the work itself, we care deeply about how we work. We believe great teams are built through collaboration, curiosity, accountability, and trust. Whether you're supporting customer missions, strengthening business operations, or leading expeditions of your own, Via Logic is a place where Explorers are encouraged to grow, contribute, and continuously evolve.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Via Logic LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace where all Explorers are valued and supported. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for engagement without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable federal, state, or local law. We believe different perspectives strengthen teams, improve innovation, and help us build better solutions for the missions we support.

Accessibility & Accommodations

Via Logic is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive hiring experience for all candidates. Reasonable accommodations are available throughout the application and interview process to support accessibility needs and ensure every candidate has an equitable opportunity to explore an engagement with our team.

Recruiting Fraud Notice

Via Logic takes recruiting fraud seriously. We will never ask candidates for payment, banking information, cryptocurrency, gift cards, or other personal financial information during any stage of the hiring process. All legitimate communication from our team will come directly from authorized Via Logic representatives using official company channels. Due to the rise of fraudulent recruiting activity across the industry, we encourage candidates to use caution if something feels unusual, rushed, or too good to be true. Real adventures should involve solving meaningful challenges—not wiring money to strangers pretending to be recruiters on the internet. If you have concerns about the legitimacy of a communication claiming to represent Via Logic, please verify the information through our official website before sharing personal information or taking further action.

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha rarely find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—sitting across a dinner table—told them, "This made a difference for our child." You will own that word-of-mouth system for an entire region: the gatherings, the parent champions, the relationship with the mayor's office, the CEO who provides a 14-year-old with their first meaningful project.

Your typical week involves four distinct environments. You create and execute the regional event calendar, ranging from 150-person open houses to eight-person curated dinners, running several each month. You identify and train current parents eager to share their experiences with prospective families, then broker one-to-one connections. You cultivate ties with municipal leaders and corporate executives, converting them into event venues, allies for campus expansions, and tangible pathways for students. And you fulfill the Alpha Networks promise: brokered introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internship placements, alumni integration, tracked meticulously family by family.

No complete playbook exists. You develop it in real time, and the frameworks you create become templates for colleagues building identical engines in other markets. As your region expands, the challenge intensifies: doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth attributable to personal endorsements, evaluated over years rather than quarters.

No degree is mandatory, and no specific background is preferred. An MBA, a career in consulting or wealth management, and a self-directed path in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight. What matters is a demonstrated history of convening people and converting relationships into outcomes.

This position is based on-site in one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. The role includes evening and weekend events with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and entrepreneurs, plus frequent local travel. You will become the most networked individual in your city, and you will invest that capital in students. If that exchange feels purposeful rather than burdensome, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and executing the regional event calendar: public open events, curated dinners segmented by city and grade level, and family retreats, multiple times per month within budget
Arranging venues, hosts, and vendors, then serving as live host during each event
Identifying current parents to serve as ambassadors, arming them with authentic narratives, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing connections with municipal officials and corporate leaders, and converting those relationships into event venues, campus launch support, and opportunities for students
Pairing enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, expert-led masterclasses, and professional internships, and integrating graduating families into the alumni network within 30 days
Recording every event, introduction, and referral source in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) to ensure "doors opened per family" is measurable and accurate

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth. No paid advertising, no media budget, no impression or lead-generation metrics
Managing brand narrative or centralized campaigns; that belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions logistics, conducting tours, or managing enrollment documentation; Admissions and Family Success own that
Operating a campus on a daily basis, or managing the physical facility
Presenting raw attendance figures and headcount as if a filled room were the objective
Waiting for a finalized playbook, a template, or additional staff before launching

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Drive people-driven referrals as the primary source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years creating communities or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or similar network businesses, where growth originated from people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client portfolio, with quantifiable results
Personally planned and executed 20+ events spanning the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ attendee open events, with full budget responsibility
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or corporate executives that delivered specific, identifiable value
Consistent CRM practitioner; tracking relationships, attributions, and activities is already standard practice
Currently resides in, or willing to relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Eligible to work in the US without requiring visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community, or partnership initiatives for a network-structured organization: a school network, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic body
Developed and leveraged a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Advanced through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and consistently served as the institutional representative and host
Pre-existing connections with local government or the business ecosystem in your city
Deep understanding of how families navigate high-stakes education choices

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

Position Details

Position Information

Dean, College of Letters & Science

406-994-4288

Classification Title Executive Director Working Title Executive Director, QCORE Brief Position Overview

QCORE seeks a strategic leader to build and sustain an organization that advances research and scientific discovery.

Position Number 4C0093 Department Physics Division College of Letters & Science Appointment Type Professional Contract Term Fiscal Year Semester If other, specify From date If other, specify End date FLSA Exempt Union Affiliation Exempt from Collective Bargaining FTE 1.0 Benefits Eligible Eligible Salary Salary commensurate with experience, education, and qualifications. Contract Type LOA If other, please specify Recruitment Type Open

Position Details

General Statement

The Executive Director of QCORE serves as the head of a university-wide research institute and works closely with affiliated faculty and staff to build and lead a successful program advancing research and scientific discovery in quantum science, engineering, and business.

QCORE’s primary objective is to empower Montana’s quantum ecosystem by uniting cutting-edge research, industry partnerships, and community engagement – enabling breakthrough technologies that shape the future of quantum innovation. The vision of QCORE is to lead Montana’s transformation into a global powerhouse for quantum-enabled technologies by 2035, fostering economic growth, academic excellence and a resilient, future-focused workforce.

QCORE exists to steward the development of transformative quantum technologies in service to the common good. QCORE will help students plan for careers in quantum and quantum-enabling systems and will support transitioning into those careers through strategic partnerships with Montana’s growing quantum industry. Strategic partnerships serve as the mechanism for QCORE to strengthen relationships between industry, research and innovators – growing collaboration and creating shared opportunities for beneficial technology innovations.

Pending approval of research center status, QCORE is housed in The College of Letters & Science (CLS), the largest center for learning, teaching and research at Montana State University. CLS offers students an excellent liberal arts and sciences education in nearly 50 majors, 25 minors and over 25 graduate degrees within the four areas of the humanities, natural sciences, mathematical, and social sciences.

Building on the great strength of our traditional disciplines, the college provides exciting opportunities for faculty and students at the cutting edge of interdisciplinary inquiry. CLS is dedicated to supporting student success, discovering and disseminating new knowledge, and providing an atmosphere in which discovery and learning are integrated and valued. CLS is at the confluence of intellectual tradition, discovery, and innovation.

When research center status is finalized for QCORE, the center will be in the Office of the Vice President for Research and Economic Development.

Duties and Responsibilities

Strategically position QCORE to be a nationally recognized, best-in-class research and development center for advancement of quantum technology, a leader in quantum workforce development and a deeply integrated innovation ecosystem that supports the translation of quantum and related technologies to industry.
Develop and implement long-term strategies to improve QCORE’s overall sustainability, effectiveness, and responsiveness to the needs of sponsoring organizations and companies in the state, region, nation, and internationally.
Develop and maintain a best-in-class governance structure for QCORE.
Build and nurture long-term relationships with key stakeholders, including federal agencies, individual donors, institutional funders, congressional representatives, and corporate partners.
Build strategic alliances and partnerships with other testbeds, academic institutions, corporations, and governments to expand QCORE’s reach, visibility, and impact.
Lead efforts to secure sustainable funding through partnerships, campaigns, and new initiatives to diversify the organization’s revenue (e.g., federal and private grants, federal cooperative awards, donations, industrial partnerships, social enterprises). This includes engagement with our legislature.
Participate in sector-specific organizations relevant to quantum technologies and quantum supply chain, including standards development and testbed communities of practice. Present at national and international gatherings of experts in these respective fields.
Leads efforts to ensure that QCORE remains a vital part of MSU’s land-grant mission, promoting quantum science and economic development in Montana, the region, and nation, and providing practical learning opportunities for students.
Support QCORE faculty and scientists seeking and obtaining external funding to promote innovation, discovery, and dissemination of quantum science and technology.
Ensure operational excellence, overseeing all aspects of budgeting, accounting, personnel, facilities, security, and safety.
Ensure that QCORE complies with all legal, regulatory, safety, and ethical standards at local, national, and international levels.
Ensure that QCORE meets all required grant reporting requirements.
Coordinate with QCORE’s leadership team to lead and mentor staff, fostering a positive, collaborative, and mission-driven organizational culture.
Oversee the monitoring and evaluation of program outcomes to measure success and inform future strategies at a national and international level.
Prioritize sustainability in all programs and initiatives, ensuring long-term environmental, social, and financial viability.

Required Qualifications – Experience, Education, Knowledge & Skills

PhD in Physics, Engineering, or a related field, or a terminal degree with equivalent industry experience.
Demonstrated experience in strategic leadership of a research center or related entity, or business.
Demonstrated experience in federal research grant-seeking, fundraising, or business development.

Preferred Qualifications – Experience, Education, Knowledge & Skills

A demonstrated record of scientific or business innovation.
Demonstrated experience with technology transfer.
Experience navigating or contributing to the mission of a land-grant university, including economic development, outreach, and workforce training.

The Successful Candidate Will

Have knowledge of the disciplines and programs represented in QCORE and a commitment to our vision.
A record of positive staff and personnel relations and interactions.
A creative and approachable manner that kindles the innovative spirit of others.
A strong ability to communicate effectively as exemplified by the candidates’ writing, speaking, and listening skills.
Demonstrated accomplishments in research, scholarship, and innovative partnerships.

Position Special Requirements/Additional Information

This position is contingent upon continued grant funding.

This is a full-time position with extensive travel required for regional, national, and international events and partnership meetings. Occasional evening and weekend work may be required to support onsite event management.

Successful candidate must be able to comply with the federally mandated requirements of U.S. export control laws, which may require proof that candidate is a U.S. citizen.

All QCORE employees may be required to meet NIST 800-53 requirements for access to Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). This position may require the ability to obtain a DoD Security Clearance.

This job description should not be construed as an exhaustive statement of duties, responsibilities or requirements, but a general description of the job. Nothing contained herein restricts Montana State University’s rights to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

By joining the American Red Cross you will touch millions of lives every year and experience the greatness of the human spirit at its best. Are you ready to be part of the world's largest humanitarian network?

Join us—Where your Career is a Force for Good!

Job Description

Joining the American Red Cross is like nothing else – it’s as much something you feel as something you do. You become a vital part of the world’s largest humanitarian network. Joining a team of welcoming individuals who are exceptional yet unassuming. Diverse, yet uncompromising in unity. You grow your career within a movement that matters, where success is measured in people helped, communities made whole, and individuals equipped to never stop changing lives and situations for the better.

When you choose to be a force for good, you’ll have mentors who empower your growth along a purposeful career path. You align your life’s work with an ongoing mission that’s bigger than all of us. As you care for others, you’re cared for with competitive compensation and benefits. You join a community that respects who you are away from work as much as what you do while at work.

Where Your Career is a Force for Good!

The American Red Cross is seeking a Chief Development Officer
to support the California Gold Country Region. This region supports 31 counties in Northern California. This is a hybrid position. Incumbents will spend several days a week in the office and the remainder of their time in the field or in a home office.

What You Need To Know

In this role, you will lead a team of professional fundraisers to strengthen and grow the region’s donor base to meet its assigned financial target of more than $10M. The Chief Development Officer will provide leadership to the staff and volunteers in planning, managing, and implementing fundraising development strategies for the assigned segment(s) of giving. They will also assist in cultivating donors and sponsors to meet monthly, quarterly, and annual revenue targets while maintaining their own portfolios. The Director is responsible for managing an assigned team, including hiring, training, coaching, evaluating, and managing performance. This role is not eligible for relocation assistance.

Where Your Career Is a Force Good

Manage a portfolio of high-level donors and prospects within the assigned segment to achieve the annual revenue target, including both renewable gifts and new incremental revenue.
Develop and implement a plan for revenue growth from donors at the $5,000+ level with an emphasis on maximizing revenue for the American Red Cross. The individual segment will collaborate with the Gift Planning team to strategically grow planned giving revenue across major donor-managed accounts for individuals and families. The corporate and foundation segments’ strategic growth plan could include (but are not limited to) engagement and growth of giving societies such as the Tiffany Circle, serving as a staff liaison to the Board's Philanthropy Committee and developing and implementing strategies for board giving and influence for the region, growing cause marketing and overall corporate revenue by assisting corporations in achieving their goals to strengthen their brand, marketing, and employee engagement, leading the region's special events program, or leading a strategy to identify, cultivate, and engage foundations to grow their support for the American Red Cross.
Cultivate relationships and serve as primary staff liaison for major donors and conduct regular joint visits with relationship managers and donors when those relationships are managed by members of your team.
Collaborate with national headquarters development team members to maximize fundraising opportunities and implement policies and procedures to ensure the success of the region's fundraising efforts.
Oversee the implementation of organizational campaigns in the region.
Serve as a senior leader in the Region and proactively drive the implementation of strategic decisions for the organization. Ensure that the Region meets all reporting requirements related to fundraising, including ensuring up-to-date donor records in Salesforce.
Provide strong leadership, develop, and set individual and team performance goals and manage/drive change.
Hire, manage, train, and evaluate staff and volunteers to ensure fundraising results and that all team members meet or exceed national/regional fundraising metrics.
Lead and execute disaster relief fundraising efforts as appropriate.

What You Need To Succeed

Education:
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required.

Experience:
Minimum 7 years of sales/fundraising experience or equivalent combination of education and related experience required. Experience with increasing philanthropic revenue from diverse constituencies, developing and implementing broad-based fundraising programs, and knowledge of “best practices” in development.

Management Experience:
5 years of management experience.

Skills & Abilities:
Ability to relate well and work effectively with multiple constituencies and audiences. Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written skills. Knowledge of office systems: MS Office preferred and fundraising database systems (e.g. Raiser’s Edge, Salesforce.com). Ability to work on a team within a collaborative environment and ensure the highest customer service orientation.

Travel:
Requires frequent travel within the Region. The amount will vary depending upon size and geography of region. Occasional travel within the Division may be required.

Drive:
A current, valid driver's license and a good driving record are required.

Physical Requirements:
Physical requirements are those present in normal office environment conditions. Operational flexibility is required to meet sudden and unpredictable needs. Ability to use a personal computer, applicable software, and office equipment for sustained periods of time. May include sitting for long periods of time, driving a vehicle, and working under challenging conditions.

What Will Give You The Competitive Edge

Strong leadership/ coaching experience

Proven fundraising experience in Northern California

Effective relationship builder

Salary Information

The salary range for this position is $129,000- $142,000.

Note that the American Red Cross sets salary ranges aligned to a specific geographic location in which the work is performed. The stated salary range in this posting is an average. The specific salary information will be shared at the time of phone screening based upon your location and qualifications.

Benefits For You

As a mission-based organization, we believe our team needs great support to do great work. Our comprehensive package includes:

Medical, Dental, and Vision plans
Health Spending Accounts & Flexible Spending Accounts
PTO: Starting 15 days a year; based on type of job and tenure
Holidays: 11 paid holidays comprised of six core holidays and five floating holidays
401K with up to 6% match
Paid Family Leave Employee Assistance
Disability and Insurance: Short + Long Term
Service Awards and recognition

Apply now! Joining our team will provide you with the opportunity to

make your career a force for good!

Organization Overview

The Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) and Performance Racing Industry (PRI) together represent the heart of the automotive aftermarket and motorsports industries. United by a passion for cars, trucks, SUVs, and racing of every kind, these organizations support a vibrant global marketplace that spans performance parts, advanced racing technologies, restoration, restyling, and the full spectrum of specialty automotive innovation.

SEMA is a dynamic, business-minded nonprofit trade association made up of manufacturers, distributors, retailers, builders, publishers, race teams, and more—an industry ecosystem powering a nearly $53-billion-a-year retail market. Through industry-leading programs, advocacy, research, and world-class events—including the annual SEMA Show, one of the largest automotive trade shows in the world—SEMA helps its members grow, innovate, and succeed.

PRI extends this influence into the global racing marketplace. Since 1986, PRI has been the premier source of business intelligence, cutting-edge technology insights, and community connection for racing professionals. The annual PRI Trade Show in Indianapolis brings together over 1,000 exhibiting companies and thousands of racing stakeholders across every major discipline, supported by PRI’s industry-leading advocacy, media platforms, education programs, and year-round engagement.

Together, SEMA and PRI fuel the success of thousands of businesses, connect industry professionals worldwide, and preserve and grow the future of automotive performance and racing.

Key executive leader responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the Association. Establish, monitor, evaluate and report on Annual Association Goals. Responsibilities include, preparation for CEO of periodic BOD report and Annual FY Association Goal Report for CEO and BOD leadership. (In conjunction with VP of Administration/CFO)

Perform other assignments and duties as required by CEO.

Reports to CEO.
Interfaces with Vice Presidents/Directors/employees/Board of Directors.
Interfaces with the Association members and prospective members.

Excellent written and oral communication skills with proven public speaking and managerial skills.
Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks.

new_jobs.title: Director of Advancement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha seldom find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—across a dinner table or during a conversation—told them, "This made a real difference for my child." Your responsibility is to own that word-of-mouth engine for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassador network, the relationships with civic leaders, the CEO who creates a pathway for a 14-year-old's first meaningful project.

In a typical week, you will be present in four different rooms. You will design and execute the region's event calendar, from a 150-guest open house to an intimate eight-person dinner, hosting several each month. You will identify and recruit current parents who are genuinely eager to share their experience with prospective families, and you will facilitate those one-to-one connections. You will cultivate relationships with city officials and business leaders, converting them into event venues, advocates for new campus launches, and tangible opportunities for students. And you will deliver on the Alpha Networks promise: introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internships, alumni transitions—tracked family by family.

There is no complete playbook waiting for you. You will create it as you go, and the systems you develop will be adopted by colleagues building the same infrastructure in other cities. As the region expands, the challenge intensifies rather than simplifies: the number of doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth that comes from real people advocating for Alpha, assessed over years rather than quarters.

No specific degree or credential is required. An MBA, a background in consulting or wealth management, or a self-built career in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight here. What matters is your demonstrated ability to bring people together and convert those relationships into measurable outcomes.

This role is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Evenings and weekends spent in rooms with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and entrepreneurs are standard, as is frequent local travel. You will become the most networked person in your city, and you will invest that capital in the service of students. If that exchange feels like the purpose rather than the price, you should apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and executing the region's event calendar: open gatherings, curated dinners organized by city and grade level, and family retreats, managing several per month within budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then serving as the live host for each event
Recruiting current parents to serve as ambassadors, equipping them with authentic stories, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing relationships with public officials and business executives, and converting those relationships into venues, support for campus expansion, and opportunities for students
Connecting enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and transitioning graduating families into alumni status within 30 days
Recording every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM so that "doors opened per family" reflects an accurate, trackable metric

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth through paid media, ad spend, or impression and lead-volume metrics
Controlling the brand narrative or top-level campaigns; that responsibility belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions processing, conducting tours, or managing enrollment paperwork; those are owned by Admissions and Family Success
Operating a campus on a day-to-day basis, or managing the physical facility
Treating raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the measure of success
Waiting for a completed playbook, templated materials, or support staff before beginning your work

Director Of Advancement Key Responsibilities

Drive people-first referrals as the majority source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or a comparable network business, where growth was generated through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with measurable results
Personal experience designing and executing 20+ gatherings across the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget accountability
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or business executives that resulted in concrete, identifiable value
Disciplined CRM usage; tracking relationships, attributions, and actions is an existing practice
Currently resides in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without requiring visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community building, or partnerships for a network-oriented organization: a school network, membership club, franchise, or civic or faith-based institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Rose through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were consistently chosen to host and represent the organization
Established relationships with local government or business leaders in your city
Deep understanding of how families make high-stakes educational decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $200 USD/hour, which equates to $400,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

new_jobs.title: Managing Director & Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments
new_jobs.description:
Your opportunity

Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments

Overview

The Managing Director & Head of Private Assets and Alternative Investments will report to the Chief Executive Officer of Schwab Asset Management and lead a team responsible for managing our expanding portfolio of non-traditional investment management offerings including the planned launch of the Schwab Private Company Fund.

Key Outcomes

This leader will be accountable for establishing the strategic direction, investment governance, operating model, and risk discipline required to scale Schwab’s private assets and alternative investments platform. The role requires sound independent judgment within approved investment guidelines, strong executive presence, and the ability to connect investment strategy, product innovation, risk management, and client outcomes across SAM/CSIM and the broader Schwab enterprise.

Set the long-term strategic agenda for Private Assets and Alternative Investments, including portfolio construction philosophy, product roadmap, governance standards, risk controls, and operating discipline across current and future offerings.
Lead the successful development, launch, and scaling of the Schwab Private Company Fund and related offerings, ensuring investment design, legal structure, compliance oversight, operations, distribution readiness, and client experience are aligned from concept through commercialization.
Make independent investment and business decisions within approved guidelines, balancing growth, liquidity, valuation, manager selection, operational complexity, fiduciary obligations, regulatory expectations, and Schwab’s reputation for client-first stewardship.
Oversee risk across the Private Assets and Alternative Investments platform, partnering closely with Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, and Technology teams to ensure strong controls, clear accountability, scalable processes, and effective issue escalation.
Serve as a senior investment and business advisor to the Chief Executive Officer of SAM/CSIM and the broader executive team, providing informed perspectives on private markets, alternative investment trends, fund performance, competitive dynamics, product opportunities, and enterprise implications.
Represent the platform with credibility before the Funds Board of Directors, SAM/CSIM committees, firm-wide risk committees, regulators, and senior enterprise stakeholders, translating complex investment, liquidity, valuation, and governance topics into clear executive-level recommendations.
Partner with leadership on the construction and oversight of SPVs serving as building blocks for the Schwab Private Company Fund, ensuring close coordination across sourcing, due diligence, structuring, valuation, operational readiness, and ongoing monitoring.
Provide leadership and expertise to third-party investment oversight and asset allocation forums involving private assets, helping shape manager due diligence, allocation recommendations, risk evaluation, and governance practices across Schwab’s expanding alternatives ecosystem.
Build, develop, and retain a high-performing team of investment professionals, portfolio managers, and research talent, strengthening bench depth, decision quality, accountability, and collaboration across an evolving and strategically important platform.
Drive medium- and long-term process improvement initiatives enhancing investment rigor, reporting transparency, regulatory readiness, operational scalability, and confidence among clients, advisors, boards, regulators, and enterprise partners.

What you have

Required Experience

15+ years of progressive senior investment leadership experience across private markets, alternative investments, asset management, portfolio construction, manager research, fund governance, or related investment disciplines.
Deep expertise investing in, allocating to, or overseeing private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, venture capital, secondaries, co-investments, hedge funds, or other alternative investment strategies, with strong judgment across multiple market cycles.
Demonstrated command of private markets portfolio construction, manager due diligence, valuation practices, liquidity management, risk oversight, investment committee governance, and ongoing monitoring of complex, less-liquid investment vehicles.
Proven knowledge of registered fund structures and regulatory requirements, including 1940 Act funds, interval funds, tender-offer funds, business development companies, registered alternatives, and other vehicles designed to broaden access to private market strategies.
Track record leading the development, approval, launch, and commercialization of new investment products, coordinating investment, legal, compliance, operations, finance, product, technology, distribution, and client-facing stakeholders through complex execution milestones.
Experience engaging with boards, regulators, senior executives, risk committees, investment committees, and external partners on investment strategy, governance, valuation, liquidity, risk controls, regulatory readiness, and client impact.
Strong understanding of the operational, legal, compliance, tax, reporting, and technology considerations required to support private assets and alternative investments at scale in a highly regulated financial services environment.
Proven people leadership capability, including the ability to recruit and develop investment talent, set clear expectations, build succession depth, strengthen team operating discipline, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, sound judgment, and continuous improvement.

Key Experiences & Ideal Profile

The ideal candidate is a seasoned private markets and alternative investments leader with the investment credibility, enterprise judgment, and executive presence to scale a strategically important platform within a complex, highly regulated financial services firm. This individual brings both strategic vision and practical execution discipline, with a demonstrated ability to set direction, lead through ambiguity, build durable governance, and translate sophisticated investment concepts into clear decisions for executives, boards, regulators, advisors, and clients.

Key leadership attributes include sound judgment, high integrity, intellectual rigor, executive presence, strong organizational discipline, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders through credibility, clarity, and trust. The leader must be comfortable operating at the intersection of investment management, product innovation, risk governance, legal and regulatory requirements, operations, distribution, and enterprise strategy while creating alignment across teams with different priorities and accountabilities.

Strategic, client-focused leader who can shape Schwab’s point of view on private assets and alternatives while maintaining disciplined stewardship, transparency, and risk management consistent with Schwab’s values.
Credible investment professional with deep private markets expertise and the ability to evaluate opportunities, risks, managers, structures, valuations, liquidity considerations, and portfolio implications with rigor and independence.
Collaborative enterprise leader who builds trusted relationships across SAM/CSIM, Schwab Risk, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, Product, Distribution, Technology, Forge Global Advisors, SIPSS, external managers, regulators, and board-level stakeholders.
An inclusive people leader who can elevate a specialized team, develop future leaders, reinforce accountability, and create a culture that combines intellectual rigor, prudent risk-taking, operational excellence, high engagement, and continuous learning.
Decisive and balanced executive who can make sound calls amid incomplete information, competing priorities, market uncertainty, regulatory complexity, and evolving client needs while maintaining appropriate escalation, transparency, and governance discipline.
Change leader who can bring structure to ambiguity, mobilize cross-functional teams, build confidence in new investment capabilities, and guide the organization through the operational, cultural, and governance changes required to scale private assets responsibly.
Cisciplined operator who can establish scalable processes, governance routines, reporting frameworks, issue escalation protocols, and decision forums to support growth in a complex and evolving investment category.
An executive communicator who can simplify complexity, provide balanced recommendations, and represent the platform with confidence in senior leadership meetings, committee settings, board discussions, regulatory interactions, and industry forums.

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time for vacation, volunteering, and 28-day sabbatical after every 5 years of service for eligible positions
Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement
Health, dental, and vision insurance

: Director of Operations

Position Summary

Chadwick School is accepting applications for a newly created position entitled Director of Operations (DOO). The DOO is an administrative leader responsible for the strategic oversight, coordination, and continuous improvement of essential non-academic operational functions that support the mission, safety, and daily life of the school community. Serving approximately 850 students and 200 employees across a 45-acre campus, including 21 faculty/staff residential housing units, the Director helps ensure that operational services are safe, efficient, compliant, responsive, and aligned with the school's educational priorities and institutional values.

The Director of Operations reports directly to the Chief Financial Officer/Chief Operating Officer (CFO/COO) and serves as a member of the school's senior administrative leadership team. The DOO will collaborate with the Business Office, facilities department, department directors, staff, academic leaders, families, consultants, regulatory agencies, vendors, and community stakeholders to maintain a safe and thriving learning environment and to support the school's strategic priorities.

This position is designed as a strategic operational leadership role with increasing responsibility over time. Working in close partnership with the CFO/COO, the Director of Operations will assume progressively broader leadership responsibilities across the school's operational functions as part of the school's long-term leadership succession strategy.

Essential Responsibilities

Campus Safety and Security

Provide strategic leadership and oversight of all campus safety and security operations
Review, implement, and regularly evaluate comprehensive safety, emergency preparedness, and crisis response plans, and will revise as needed
Coordinate emergency drills, tabletop exercises, and incident response procedures.
Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations related to campus safety and emergency management
Serve as a member of the school's emergency response and crisis management teams.
Oversee security personnel, visitor management systems, access control systems, and campus surveillance technologies
Oversee emergency communications systems and protocols, including mass notification platforms and emergency messaging procedures
Partner with school leadership to promote a culture of safety, preparedness, and situational awareness throughout the community.

Environmental Health and Safety (EHS)

Provide support for the school's environmental health and safety programs and regulatory compliance efforts
Coordinate compliance activities related to workplace safety requirements and applicable environmental regulations
Partner with Facilities, Human Resources, Health and Academic Departments to identify, assess, and mitigate environmental and occupational risks
Support safety training initiatives and maintain appropriate documentation and reporting processes
Monitor evolving regulatory requirements and recommend operational improvements to maintain compliance and reduce risk exposure

Mail Services

Direct Liaison with representatives from USPS, FedEx, Amazon, and other services
Oversee campus mail operations, package management, and distribution systems, revising as needed in conjunction with Facilities and other departments
Ensure efficient processing and delivery of internal and external mail, parcels, and special deliveries
Develop procedures to support increasing package volumes associated with residential housing and campus operations

Food Services

Direct Liaison with onsite school dining service representatives
Partner with CFO/COO to oversee school dining services and relationships with food service providers
Monitor operational performance, food quality, customer service, and regulatory compliance in close partnership with dining service representative, facilities department and school leadership
Partner with dining provider to support student wellness initiatives, dietary accommodations, sustainability goals, and community events.
Review and manage service contracts, budgets, and operational metrics in partnership with the CFO/COO

Logistics and Campus Operations Support

Collaborate with the Facilities Director to help coordinate major operational logistics for school events, ceremonies, summer and community programs, and special initiatives
Develop systems and procedures that improve operational efficiency and service delivery
Collaborate with facilities, advancement and academic departments to support evolving campus needs

Enterprise Risk Management and Business Continuity

Partner with the CFO/COO in leading the school's enterprise risk management program
Support the identification, assessment, and monitoring of strategic, operational, financial, reputational, and compliance risks across the institution
Support the development and implementation of mitigation strategies and risk reporting processes for the senior leadership team and the Board of Trustees
